sentences.zh: 五行傳曰：「棄法律，逐功臣，殺太子，以妾為妻，則火不炎上。

translations.literal: The Tradition of the Five Elements says: "If one abandons the laws, expels meritorious ministers, kills the crown prince, and takes a concubine as wife, then fire will not flame upward."
translations.idiomatic: The Tradition of the Five Elements states: "When the ruler casts aside law, drives out worthy ministers, slays the heir apparent, and elevates a concubine to wife, fire loses its power to blaze upward."

sentences.zh: 」謂火失其性而為災也。

translations.literal: " This means fire loses its nature and becomes a disaster.
translations.idiomatic: " That is, fire abandons its proper nature and calamity follows.

sentences.zh: 又曰：「視之不明，是謂不哲。

translations.literal: It also says: "If vision is unclear, this is called lack of wisdom."
translations.idiomatic: It further says: "When sight fails, that is called want of discernment."

sentences.zh: 厥咎舒，厥罰恒懊，厥極疾。

translations.literal: Its fault is laxity; its punishment is constant distress; its ultimate limit is illness.
translations.idiomatic: The fault is indulgence; the penalty is unending sorrow; the extreme is disease.

sentences.zh: 時則有草妖，時則有臝蟲之孽，時則有羊禍，時則有目痾，時則有赤眚、赤祥。

translations.literal: At such times there are grass prodigies; at such times calamities of naked creatures; at such times sheep disasters; at such times diseases of the eyes; at such times red disasters and red portents.
translations.idiomatic: In such seasons one finds ominous grasses, plagues of skin-bearing creatures, calamities involving sheep, disorders of the eyes, and red disasters and red omens.

sentences.zh: 惟水沴火。

translations.literal: Only water harms fire.
translations.idiomatic: Water alone is what afflicts fire.

sentences.zh: 」臝蟲，劉歆傳以為羽蟲。

translations.literal: " Naked creatures—in Liu Xin's tradition are taken to be feathered creatures.
translations.idiomatic: " As for naked creatures, Liu Xin's tradition interprets them as feathered creatures.

sentences.zh: 火不炎上

translations.literal: Fire not flaming upward
translations.idiomatic: Fire Fails to Flame Upward

sentences.zh: 魏明帝太和五月，清商殿災。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the Taihe era of Emperor Ming of Wei, the Qingshang Hall burned.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of Emperor Ming of Wei's Taihe reign, fire destroyed the Qingshang Hall.

sentences.zh: 初，帝為平原王，納河南虞氏為妃。

translations.literal: Earlier, when the emperor was Prince of Pingyuan, he took Lady Yu of Henan as consort.
translations.idiomatic: Before his accession, while he was still Prince of Pingyuan, he married Lady Yu of Henan as his consort.

sentences.zh: 及即位，不以為后，更立典虞車工卒毛嘉女，是為悼皇后。

translations.literal: When he took the throne, he did not make her empress, but instead installed the daughter of Mao Jia, a chariot-craft foreman under the Director of Imperial Parks, who became Empress Dao.
translations.idiomatic: After he came to the throne he did not raise her to empress, but set up instead the daughter of Mao Jia, a chariot-yard foreman in the Directorate of Parks, as Empress Dao.

sentences.zh: 后本仄微，非所宜升。

translations.literal: The empress's origins were humble and low; it was not fitting that she be elevated.
translations.idiomatic: The new empress came from a mean station and ought not to have been raised so high.

sentences.zh: 以妾為妻之罰也。

translations.literal: This was the penalty for taking a concubine as wife.
translations.idiomatic: It was the retribution for elevating a concubine to the status of wife.

sentences.zh: 魏明帝青龍元年六月，洛陽宮鞠室災。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the first year of the Qinglong era of Emperor Ming of Wei, the cuju court in the Luoyang palace burned.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the first Qinglong year under Emperor Ming of Wei, fire struck the kickball court in the Luoyang palace.

sentences.zh: 二年四月，崇華殿災，延于南閣。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the second year, the Chonghua Hall burned, spreading to the southern gallery.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the second year the Chonghua Hall caught fire and the blaze spread to the southern wing.

sentences.zh: 繕復之。

translations.literal: It was repaired and restored.
translations.idiomatic: The hall was rebuilt.

sentences.zh: 至三年七月，此殿又災。

translations.literal: By the seventh month of the third year, this hall burned again.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the third year the same hall burned once more.

sentences.zh: 帝問高堂隆：「此何咎也？

translations.literal: The emperor asked Gao Tanglong: "What fault does this signify?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked Gao Tanglong, "What does this omen mean?"

sentences.zh: 於禮寧有祈禳之義乎？

translations.literal: According to ritual, is there any meaning in praying and exorcising?"
translations.idiomatic: Does ritual propriety call for prayers of supplication here?"

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「夫災變之發，皆所以明教誡也。

translations.literal: " He replied: "When disasters and anomalies arise, it is always to make clear a lesson of admonition."
translations.idiomatic: " He answered, "Heaven sends calamities and strange events precisely to teach and warn."

sentences.zh: 唯率禮修德，可以勝之。

translations.literal: Only by leading with ritual and cultivating virtue can one overcome them.
translations.idiomatic: Only by observing ritual and cultivating virtue can they be overcome.

sentences.zh: 易傳曰：『上不儉，下不節，孽火燒其室。

translations.literal: The Tradition of the Changes says: 'If the superior is not frugal and the inferior is not restrained, calamitous fire burns his dwelling.'
translations.idiomatic: The Yi tradition says, 'When those above are not sparing and those below are not temperate, baleful fire consumes the house.'

sentences.zh: 』又曰：『君高其臺，天火為災。

translations.literal: ' It also says: 'If the lord raises his terrace high, heaven's fire becomes disaster.'
translations.idiomatic: ' It also says, 'When the ruler builds his terrace too high, heaven sends fire as calamity.'

sentences.zh: 』此人君苟飾宮室，不知百姓空竭，故天應之以旱，火從高殿起也。

translations.literal: ' When a ruler heedlessly adorns his palaces and chambers, unaware that the common people are drained empty, heaven responds with drought, and fire rises from the lofty halls.
translations.idiomatic: ' When a ruler lavishes ornament on his palaces without seeing that the people are exhausted, heaven answers with drought and fire breaks out from the high halls.

sentences.zh: 案舊占，災火之發，皆以臺榭宮室為誡。

translations.literal: According to ancient prognostications, whenever calamitous fire breaks out, it always takes terraces, pavilions, and palaces as its warning.
translations.idiomatic: Ancient divination holds that whenever disaster-fire appears, it warns against terraces, pavilions, and palaces.

sentences.zh: 今宜罷散民役，務從節約，清掃所災之處，不敢於此有所營造。

translations.literal: Now Your Majesty should dismiss corvée labor, strive for economy, sweep clean the burned site, and dare not undertake any construction there.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty should now release the people from forced labor, practice strict economy, cleanse the burned ground, and refrain from building there again.

sentences.zh: 萐莆嘉禾，必生此地，以報陛下虔恭之德。

translations.literal: Fragrant grass and excellent grain will surely spring up on this spot to repay Your Majesty's reverent and respectful virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Sacred herbs and fine grain will then spring from that ground to reward Your Majesty's sincere reverence.

sentences.zh: 」不從。

translations.literal: " The emperor did not follow this advice.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor refused to heed him.

sentences.zh: 遂復崇華殿，改曰九龍。

translations.literal: He then rebuilt the Chonghua Hall and renamed it the Nine Dragons.
translations.idiomatic: He rebuilt the Chonghua Hall anyway and renamed it the Hall of Nine Dragons.

sentences.zh: 以郡國前後言龍見者九，故以為名。

translations.literal: Because commanderies and kingdoms had reported nine sightings of dragons, he took this as the name.
translations.idiomatic: Nine dragon sightings had been reported from the provinces, and he took that as the name.

sentences.zh: 多棄法度，疲民逞欲，以妾為妻之應也。

translations.literal: He had largely abandoned law and regulation, exhausted the people to indulge his desires—the response to taking a concubine as wife.
translations.idiomatic: He had cast aside law, worn out the people to satisfy his desires—the omen answering his elevation of a concubine to wife.

sentences.zh: 吳孫亮建興元年十二月，武昌端門災。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of the first year of Jianxing under Sun Liang of Wu, the Duan Gate at Wuchang burned.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of the first Jianxing year of Sun Liang of Wu, fire destroyed the Duan Gate at Wuchang.

sentences.zh: 改作端門，又災內殿。

translations.literal: When the Duan Gate was rebuilt, the inner hall burned again.
translations.idiomatic: After the gate was rebuilt, the inner palace hall burned as well.

sentences.zh: 案春秋魯雉門及兩觀災。

translations.literal: Compare the Spring and Autumn Annals record of fire at Lu's pheasant gate and the two watch-towers.
translations.idiomatic: Compare the Spring and Autumn account of the fires at Lu's Pheasant Gate and its twin watch-towers.

sentences.zh: 董仲舒以為天意欲使定公誅季氏，若曰去其高顯而奢僭者也。

translations.literal: Dong Zhongshu held that Heaven's intent was to make Duke Ding execute the Ji clan—as if saying, remove those who are lofty, prominent, extravagant, and overstepping.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Zhongshu interpreted this as Heaven urging Duke Ding to destroy the Ji house—to remove what was lofty, showy, extravagant, and presumptuous.

sentences.zh: 漢武帝世，遼東高廟災，其說又同。

translations.literal: In the age of Emperor Wu of Han, the Gaomiao in Liaodong burned, and the explanation was the same.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Wu of Han the Gaomiao in Liaodong burned, and the interpretation was the same.

sentences.zh: 今此與二事頗類也。

translations.literal: The present case resembles these two events rather closely.
translations.idiomatic: The present disaster closely resembles both precedents.

sentences.zh: 且門者，號令所出，殿者，聽政之所。

translations.literal: Moreover, the gate is where commands issue forth; the hall is where government is heard.
translations.idiomatic: The gate is where orders are issued; the hall is where policy is deliberated.

sentences.zh: 是時諸葛恪秉政，而矜慢放肆，孫峻總禁旅，而險害終著。

translations.literal: At that time Zhuge Ke held power, arrogant, insolent, and unrestrained; Sun Jun commanded the palace guard, and his treacherous harm finally came to light.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Zhuge Ke held the government, proud and overbearing, while Sun Jun commanded the guards and his deadly scheming finally surfaced.

sentences.zh: 武昌，孫氏尊號所始，天戒若曰，宜除其貴要之首者。

translations.literal: Wuchang was where the Sun house first took its honorific title; Heaven's warning seemed to say that its foremost noble and powerful should be removed.
translations.idiomatic: Wuchang was where the Sun clan first assumed its imperial title; Heaven seemed to warn that the chief among the mighty must be cut down.

sentences.zh: 恪果喪眾殄民，峻授政於綝，綝廢亮也。

translations.literal: Ke indeed lost his armies and ruined the people; Jun handed power to Lin, and Lin deposed Liang.
translations.idiomatic: Ke did lose his forces and ruin the people; Jun transferred power to Sun Lin, and Lin deposed Liang.

sentences.zh: 或曰孫權毀徹武昌，以增太初宮，諸葛恪有遷都意，更起門殿，事非時宜，故見災也。

translations.literal: Some say that Sun Quan had dismantled Wuchang to enlarge the Taichu Palace, that Zhuge Ke intended to move the capital, and that rebuilding gate and hall was ill-timed—hence the disaster appeared.
translations.idiomatic: Others say Sun Quan had torn down Wuchang to expand the Taichu Palace, that Zhuge Ke meant to move the capital, and that rebuilding gates and halls at the wrong moment brought the calamity.

sentences.zh: 京房易傳曰：「君不思道，厥妖火燒宮。」

translations.literal: Jing Fang's Tradition of the Changes says: "If the ruler does not reflect on the Way, the anomaly is fire burning the palace."
translations.idiomatic: Jing Fang's Yi tradition says, "When the ruler neglects the Way, the omen is fire consuming the palace."

sentences.zh: 吳孫亮太平元年二月朔，建業火。

translations.literal: On the first day of the second month of the first year of Taiping under Sun Liang of Wu, Jianye burned.
translations.idiomatic: On the new moon of the second month of the first Taiping year under Sun Liang of Wu, a great fire broke out at Jianye.

sentences.zh: 人火之也。

translations.literal: It was fire set by human agency.
translations.idiomatic: The blaze was of human origin.

sentences.zh: 是秋，孫綝始秉政，矯以亮詔殺呂據、滕胤，明年，又輒殺朱異。

translations.literal: That autumn Sun Lin first seized power, forging Liang's edict to kill Lü Ju and Teng Yin; the next year he also killed Zhu Yi on his own authority.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn Sun Lin took control, forged an edict in Liang's name to execute Lü Ju and Teng Yin, and the following year killed Zhu Yi on his own authority.

sentences.zh: 棄法律、逐功臣之罰也。

translations.literal: This was the penalty for abandoning law and expelling meritorious ministers.
translations.idiomatic: It was the retribution for casting aside law and driving out worthy ministers.

sentences.zh: 吳孫休永安五年二月，白虎門北樓災。

translations.literal: In the second month of the fifth year of Yong'an under Sun Xiu of Wu, the north tower of the White Tiger Gate burned.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the fifth Yong'an year under Sun Xiu of Wu, fire destroyed the north tower of the White Tiger Gate.

sentences.zh: 六年十月，石頭小城火，燒西南百八十丈。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the sixth year, the small fortress at Shitou burned, consuming one hundred eighty zhang of the southwest quarter.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of the sixth year fire swept the small citadel at Shitou, burning one hundred eighty zhang along the southwest.

sentences.zh: 是時嬖人張布專擅國勢，多行無禮，而韋昭、盛冲終斥不用，兼遣察戰等為使，驚擾州郡，致使交趾反亂。

translations.literal: At that time the favorite Zhang Bu monopolized state power and often acted without propriety, while Wei Zhao and Sheng Chong were finally rejected and not employed; he also sent Cha Zhan and others as envoys, alarming and harassing commanderies and districts, causing Jiaozhi to rebel.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the favorite Zhang Bu dominated the government and behaved lawlessly, while Wei Zhao and Sheng Chong were kept from office; he also dispatched Cha Zhan and others as envoys, unsettling the provinces until Jiaozhi rose in revolt.

sentences.zh: 是其咎也。

translations.literal: This was its fault.
translations.idiomatic: That was the offense behind the omen.

sentences.zh: 吳孫晧建衡二年三月，大火，燒萬餘家，死者七百人。

translations.literal: In the third month of the second year of Jianheng under Sun Hao of Wu, a great fire burned more than ten thousand households; seven hundred people died.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the second Jianheng year under Sun Hao of Wu a conflagration destroyed more than ten thousand homes and killed seven hundred people.

sentences.zh: 案春秋，齊火。

translations.literal: Compare the Spring and Autumn Annals record of fire in Qi.
translations.idiomatic: Compare the Spring and Autumn account of the fire in Qi.

sentences.zh: 劉向以為桓公好內，聽女口，妻妾數更之罰也。

translations.literal: Liu Xiang held that Duke Huan was fond of the inner quarters, heeded women's words, and frequently changed wives and concubines—the penalty for this.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xiang interpreted it as the penalty for Duke Huan's devotion to the inner palace, his heed to women's counsel, and his constant changing of wives and concubines.

sentences.zh: 晧制令詭暴，蕩棄法度，勞臣名士，誅斥甚眾。

translations.literal: Hao's ordinances were devious and violent; he cast aside law and regulation, wore out ministers and eminent scholars, and executed or expelled very many.
translations.idiomatic: Hao's edicts were capricious and cruel; he swept away law, harried ministers and scholars, and executed or banished a great host of men.

sentences.zh: 後宮萬餘，女謁數行，其中隆寵佩皇后璽者又多矣。

translations.literal: His inner palace held more than ten thousand women; female attendants went back and forth in numbers, and among them many who received lavish favor wore the empress's seal.
translations.idiomatic: His harem held more than ten thousand women; palace women came and went in droves, and many of the most favored even bore the empress's seal.

sentences.zh: 故有大火。

translations.literal: Therefore there was the great fire.
translations.idiomatic: Hence the great conflagration.

sentences.zh: 晉武帝太康八年三月乙丑，震災西閣、楚王所止坊，及臨商觀牕。

translations.literal: On the yichou day of the third month of the eighth year of Taikang under Emperor Wu of Jin, lightning struck the western gallery, the ward where the Prince of Chu resided, and the windows of the Linshang Observatory.
translations.idiomatic: On the yichou day of the third month of the eighth Taikang year under Emperor Wu of Jin, lightning struck the western gallery, the Prince of Chu's residential ward, and the windows of the Linshang Observatory.

sentences.zh: 十年四月癸丑，崇賢殿災。

translations.literal: On the guichou day of the fourth month of the tenth year, the Chongxian Hall burned.
translations.idiomatic: On the guichou day of the fourth month of the tenth year fire destroyed the Chongxian Hall.

sentences.zh: 十月庚辰，含章鞠室、脩成堂前廡、丙坊東屋、煇章殿南閣火。

translations.literal: On the gengchen day of the tenth month, fire struck the Hanzhang cuju court, the front colonnade of the Xiucheng Hall, the eastern rooms of the Bing Ward, and the southern gallery of the Huizhang Hall.
translations.idiomatic: On the gengchen day of the tenth month fire broke out in the Hanzhang kickball court, the front veranda of the Xiucheng Hall, the eastern rooms of the Bing Ward, and the southern wing of the Huizhang Hall.

sentences.zh: 時有上書者曰：「漢王氏五侯兄弟迭任，今楊氏三公並在大位。

translations.literal: At the time a memorialist said: "Under Han the five marquises of the Wang clan held office in succession as brothers; now the three dukes of the Yang clan all hold high position together."
translations.idiomatic: A memorialist wrote at the time, "Under Han the five Wang marquises held office in turn; now the three Yang dukes all stand at the summit of power together."

sentences.zh: 天變屢見，竊為陛下憂之。

translations.literal: Heavenly changes appear repeatedly; I venture to be anxious on Your Majesty's behalf."
translations.idiomatic: Heavenly omens keep appearing, and I cannot help fearing for Your Majesty."

sentences.zh: 」楊珧由是乞退。

translations.literal: " Yang Yao therefore requested to retire.
translations.idiomatic: " Yang Yao thereupon asked to withdraw from office.

sentences.zh: 是時帝納馮紞之間，廢張華之功；

translations.literal: At that time the emperor accepted Feng Dan's private counsel and set aside Zhang Hua's achievements;
translations.idiomatic: At that time the emperor heeded Feng Dan's private advice and cast aside Zhang Hua's merits;

sentences.zh: 聽楊駿之讒，離衞瓘之寵。

translations.literal: heeded Yang Jun's slanders and estranged himself from Wei Guan's favor.
translations.idiomatic: listened to Yang Jun's slanders and turned away from Wei Guan's favor.

sentences.zh: 此逐功臣之罰也。

translations.literal: This was the penalty for expelling meritorious ministers.
translations.idiomatic: This was the retribution for driving out worthy ministers.

sentences.zh: 明年，宮車晏駕。

translations.literal: The next year the imperial carriage halted at dusk.
translations.idiomatic: The following year the emperor died.

sentences.zh: 其後楚王承竊發之旨，戮害二公，身亦不免。

translations.literal: Afterward the Prince of Chu, acting on a secretly issued directive, slaughtered the two grandees, yet he himself did not escape punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Later the Prince of Chu, acting on a clandestine order, killed the two chief ministers, yet could not save himself.

sentences.zh: 震災其坊，又天意乎。

translations.literal: Lightning had struck his ward—was this again Heaven's intent?
translations.idiomatic: Lightning had already struck his residence—was that not Heaven's intent as well?

sentences.zh: 晉惠帝元康五年閏月庚寅，武庫火。

translations.literal: On the gengyin day of the intercalary month of the fifth year of Yuankang under Emperor Hui of Jin, the armory burned.
translations.idiomatic: On the gengyin day of the intercalary fifth Yuankang year under Emperor Hui of Jin, fire destroyed the imperial armory.

sentences.zh: 張華疑有亂，先固守，然後救災。

translations.literal: Zhang Hua suspected rebellion and first held the site under guard, only then fighting the fire.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Hua, suspecting revolt, secured the site before turning to fight the blaze.

sentences.zh: 是以累代異寶，王莽頭，孔子履，漢高斷白蛇劍及二百萬人器械，一時蕩盡。

translations.literal: Thus rare treasures accumulated over generations—the head of Wang Mang, Confucius's shoe, the sword with which Gaozu of Han cut the white serpent, and arms for two million men—were swept away at once.
translations.idiomatic: Thus treasures hoarded for generations—the head of Wang Mang, Confucius's sandal, the sword with which Han Gaozu slew the white serpent, and arms for two million men—were destroyed in a single hour.

sentences.zh: 是後愍懷見殺，殺太子之罰也。

translations.literal: Afterward Prince Minhuai was killed—the penalty for slaying the crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: Later Prince Minhuai was murdered—the retribution for killing the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 天戒若曰，夫設險擊柝，所以固其國，儲積戎器，所以戒不虞。

translations.literal: Heaven's warning seemed to say: defenses and night-watch clappers are set up to secure the state; stores of weapons are amassed to guard against the unforeseen.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven seemed to warn: ramparts and watch-clappers exist to secure the realm; arsenals are stocked to guard against surprise.

sentences.zh: 今冢嗣將傾，社稷將泯，禁兵無所復施，皇旅又將誰衞。

translations.literal: Now the heir's line is about to topple, the altars of soil and grain about to perish; the palace guard can no longer be deployed, and who will guard the imperial host?
translations.idiomatic: Now the heir's house is collapsing, the altars are failing, the palace guard can no longer be used, and who will defend the throne?

sentences.zh: 帝后不悟，終喪四海，是其應也。

translations.literal: The emperor and empress did not understand; in the end they lost all within the four seas—this was the response.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor and empress failed to understand, and in the end lost the realm—the omen fulfilled.

sentences.zh: 張華、閻纂皆曰，武庫火而氐、羌反，太子見廢，則四海可知矣。

translations.literal: Zhang Hua and Yan Zuan both said: when the armory burns, the Di and Qiang rebel, and the crown prince is deposed—then the fate of all within the four seas can be known.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Hua and Yan Zuan both said that when the armory burns, the Di and Qiang rise, and the heir is deposed, the fate of the empire is already clear.

sentences.zh: 元康八年十一月，高原陵火。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of the eighth year of Yuankang, the Gaoyuan Mausoleum burned.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of the eighth Yuankang year fire struck the Gaoyuan Mausoleum.

sentences.zh: 是時賈后凶恣，賈謐擅朝，惡積罪稔，宜見誅絕。

translations.literal: At that time Empress Jia was fierce and unrestrained, Jia Mi monopolized the court; evil had accumulated and guilt was ripe—they ought to have been executed.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Empress Jia was brutal and overbearing and Jia Mi dominated the court; their crimes had piled high and they ought to have been destroyed.

sentences.zh: 天戒若曰，臣妾之不可者，雖親貴莫比，猶宜忍而誅之，如吾燔高原陵也。

translations.literal: Heaven's warning seemed to say: what must not be tolerated in ministers and consorts, though none be closer or nobler, should still be endured only long enough to execute them—as I have burned the Gaoyuan Mausoleum.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven seemed to warn that even the closest and most exalted minister or consort, when intolerable, must be struck down—as it had burned the Gaoyuan Mausoleum.

sentences.zh: 帝既眊弱，而張華又不納裴頠、劉卞之謀，故后遂與謐誣殺太子也。

translations.literal: The emperor was already dim-eyed and weak, and Zhang Hua did not adopt the plans of Pei Song and Liu Bian, so the empress then joined with Mi to frame and kill the crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was already feeble, and Zhang Hua refused the counsel of Pei Song and Liu Bian, so the empress and Mi conspired to destroy the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 干寶云：「高原陵火，太子廢，其應也。

translations.literal: Gan Bao said: "When the Gaoyuan Mausoleum burned, the crown prince was deposed—this was the response."
translations.idiomatic: Gan Bao wrote, "Fire at the Gaoyuan Mausoleum and the heir's deposition were the same omen fulfilled."

sentences.zh: 漢武帝世，高園便殿火，董仲舒對與此占同。」

translations.literal: In the age of Emperor Wu of Han, the side hall of the Gaoyuan burned; Dong Zhongshu's response used the same prognostication."
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Wu of Han the Gaoyuan side hall burned, and Dong Zhongshu's interpretation matched this reading."

sentences.zh: 晉惠帝永康元年，帝納皇后羊氏。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongkang under Emperor Hui of Jin, the emperor took Lady Yang of the Yang clan as empress.
translations.idiomatic: In the first Yongkang year under Emperor Hui of Jin the emperor married Lady Yang as empress.

sentences.zh: 后將入宮，衣中忽有火，眾咸怪之。

translations.literal: As the empress was about to enter the palace, fire suddenly appeared in her garments; all regarded it with wonder.
translations.idiomatic: As she was about to enter the palace, fire suddenly flared in her robes, and everyone was astonished.

sentences.zh: 太安二年，后父玄之以成都之逼，憂死。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tai'an, the empress's father Xuanzhi died of grief under pressure from Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: In the second Tai'an year her father Xuanzhi died of grief under pressure from the Prince of Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 永興元年，成都遂廢后，處之金墉城，而殺其叔父同之。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongxing, Chengdu then deposed the empress and confined her in Jinyong City, and also killed her uncle Tongzhi.
translations.idiomatic: In the first Yongxing year the Prince of Chengdu deposed her, confined her in Jinyong City, and killed her uncle Tongzhi.

sentences.zh: 是後還立，立而復廢者四，又詔賜死，荀藩表全之。

translations.literal: Afterward she was restored; she was enthroned and then deposed four times; an edict also ordered her to take poison, but Xun Fan memorialized to spare her life.
translations.idiomatic: She was later restored, enthroned and deposed four times, and at last ordered to take poison, though Xun Fan pleaded that her life be spared.

sentences.zh: 雖末還在位，然憂逼折辱，終古未聞。

translations.literal: Although she never finally returned to the throne, the oppression, coercion, and humiliation she suffered were unheard of since antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: Though she never held the throne again, the grief, pressure, and humiliation she endured were without precedent.

sentences.zh: 此孽火之應。

translations.literal: This was the response to the baleful fire.
translations.idiomatic: This fulfilled the omen of the baleful fire in her robes.

sentences.zh: 晉惠帝永興二年七月甲午，尚書諸曹火，延崇禮闥及閣道。

translations.literal: On the jiawu day of the seventh month of the second year of Yongxing under Emperor Hui of Jin, fire broke out in the various bureaus of the Secretariat, spreading to the Chongli gate-tower and the covered passage.
translations.idiomatic: On the jiawu day of the seventh month of the second Yongxing year under Emperor Hui of Jin, fire destroyed the Secretariat offices and spread to the Chongli gate-tower and the covered passage.

sentences.zh: 夫百揆王化之本，王者棄法律之應也。

translations.literal: The hundred offices are the root of royal transformation; this was the response to the ruler's abandonment of law.
translations.idiomatic: The hundred offices are the foundation of royal government; the blaze answered the ruler's abandonment of law.

sentences.zh: 清河王覃入為晉嗣，不終于位，又殺太子之罰也。

translations.literal: Prince Qinghe Tan entered as Jin's heir but did not complete his tenure—again the penalty for killing the crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Qinghe Tan was made heir to Jin but did not finish his tenure—again the retribution for slaying the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 晉孝懷帝永嘉四年十一月，襄陽火，死者三千餘人。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of the fourth year of Yongjia under Emperor Xiaohuai of Jin, Xiangyang burned; more than three thousand people died.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of the fourth Yongjia year under Emperor Xiaohuai of Jin a fire at Xiangyang killed more than three thousand people.

sentences.zh: 是時王如自號大將軍、司雍二州牧，眾四五萬，攻略郡縣，以為己邑。

translations.literal: At that time Wang Ru styled himself Grand General and Governor of the two provinces of Sizhou and Yongzhou; his forces numbered forty or fifty thousand, and he attacked commanderies and districts, taking them as his own territories.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Wang Ru styled himself Grand General and Governor of Sizhou and Yongzhou, mustered forty or fifty thousand men, and seized commanderies and districts for his own domain.

sentences.zh: 都督力屈，嬰城自守，賊遂攻逼襄陽。

translations.literal: The area commander exhausted his strength, clung to the city in defense, and the bandits then pressed the attack on Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: The regional commander was overmatched, shut himself within the walls, and the rebels pressed Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 此下陵上，陽失節，火災出也。

translations.literal: This was inferiors overbearing upon superiors, yang losing its proper measure—hence fire disaster appeared.
translations.idiomatic: This was the subordinate overawing the superior and yang losing its proper measure—hence the fire.

sentences.zh: 晉元帝太興中，王敦鎮武昌。

translations.literal: In the Taixing era under Emperor Yuan of Jin, Wang Dun held Wuchang as his garrison.
translations.idiomatic: During the Taixing era under Emperor Yuan of Jin, Wang Dun was stationed at Wuchang.

sentences.zh: 武昌火起，興眾救之。

translations.literal: Fire broke out at Wuchang, and he raised troops to fight it.
translations.idiomatic: When fire broke out at Wuchang he mobilized troops to fight the blaze.

sentences.zh: 救於此而發於彼，東西南北數十處俱應，數日不絕。

translations.literal: They fought the fire here, yet it broke out there; east, west, south, and north—several dozen places all responded, and for several days it did not cease.
translations.idiomatic: Men fought the blaze in one place only to see it leap up in another; fires answered one another in dozens of spots across the compass, and burned for days without end.

sentences.zh: 班固所謂濫炎妄起，雖興師不能救之之謂也。

translations.literal: This is what Ban Gu called rampant flames rising wantonly—even if one raised armies, one could not save it.
translations.idiomatic: This was what Ban Gu meant by fires raging lawlessly—no army could have quenched them.

sentences.zh: 干寶曰：「此臣而君行，亢陽失節之災也。」

translations.literal: Gan Bao said: "This is the disaster of a minister acting as ruler, of excessive yang losing its proper measure."
translations.idiomatic: Gan Bao wrote, "This was the calamity of subjects usurping the role of ruler—of overbearing yang losing its proper season."

sentences.zh: 晉元帝永昌二年正月癸巳，京都大火。

translations.literal: On the guisi day of the first month of the second year of Yongchang under Emperor Yuan of Jin, a great fire broke out in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: On the guisi day of the first month of the second Yongchang year under Emperor Yuan of Jin, the capital burned.

sentences.zh: 三月，饒安、東光、安陵三縣火，燒七千餘家，死者萬五千人。

translations.literal: In the third month, fire struck the three counties of Rao'an, Dongguang, and Anling, burning more than seven thousand households; fifteen thousand people died.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month fires in Rao'an, Dongguang, and Anling destroyed more than seven thousand homes and killed fifteen thousand people.

sentences.zh: 晉明帝太寧元年正月，京都火。

translations.literal: In the first month of the first year of Taining under Emperor Ming of Jin, the capital burned.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the first Taining year under Emperor Ming of Jin, fire struck the capital.

sentences.zh: 是時王敦威侮朝廷，多行無禮，內外臣下，咸懷怨毒。

translations.literal: At that time Wang Dun's power insulted the court; he often acted without propriety, and ministers within and without all harbored resentment and malice.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Wang Dun's might humiliated the throne, he behaved lawlessly, and courtiers everywhere nursed bitter resentment.

sentences.zh: 極陰生陽，故有火災。

translations.literal: Extreme yin gave birth to yang; therefore there was fire disaster.
translations.idiomatic: When yin reaches its extreme it generates yang—hence the fire.

sentences.zh: 與董仲舒說春秋陳火同事也。

translations.literal: This was the same matter as Dong Zhongshu's explanation of the fire in Chen in the Spring and Autumn Annals.
translations.idiomatic: It matched Dong Zhongshu's reading of the Chen fire in the Spring and Autumn Annals.

sentences.zh: 晉穆帝永和五年六月，震災石虎太武殿及兩廂、端門，光爛照天，金石皆盡，火月餘乃滅。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the fifth year of Yonghe under Emperor Mu of Jin, lightning struck Shi Hu's Taiwu Hall and its two wings and the Duan Gate; the brilliance lit the sky, metal and stone were all consumed, and the fire burned for more than a month before it died.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the fifth Yonghe year under Emperor Mu of Jin, lightning destroyed Shi Hu's Taiwu Hall, its wings, and the Duan Gate; the blaze lit the heavens, consumed metal and stone, and burned for more than a month.

sentences.zh: 是年四月，石虎死矣。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of that year, Shi Hu had already died.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Hu had died that April.

sentences.zh: 其後胡遂滅亡。

translations.literal: Afterward the barbarians were finally destroyed and perished.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward the barbarian state was destroyed.

sentences.zh: 晉海西太和中，郗愔為會稽。

translations.literal: In the Taihe era under Emperor Haixi of Jin, Xi Yin was governor of Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: During the Taihe era under Emperor Haixi of Jin, Xi Yin governed Kuaiji.

sentences.zh: 六月，大旱災，火燒數千家，延及山陰倉米數百萬斛。

translations.literal: In the sixth month there was great drought disaster; fire burned several thousand households and spread to several million hu of grain in the Shanyin granary.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month severe drought brought fire that destroyed thousands of homes and reached millions of hu of grain stored at Shanyin.

sentences.zh: 炎烟蔽天，不可撲滅。

translations.literal: Flames and smoke veiled the sky; it could not be extinguished.
translations.idiomatic: Flames and smoke blotted out the sky and could not be put out.

sentences.zh: 晉孝武帝寧康元年三月，京都風，火大起。

translations.literal: In the third month of the first year of Ningkang under Emperor Xiaowu of Jin, wind struck the capital and a great fire rose.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the first Ningkang year under Emperor Xiaowu of Jin, wind swept the capital and a great fire broke out.

sentences.zh: 是時桓溫入朝，志在陵上，少主踐位，人懷憂恐。

translations.literal: At that time Huan Wen entered court; his intent was to overawe the throne; the young lord had just taken his seat, and people harbored worry and fear.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Huan Wen had come to court with designs on the throne; the young emperor had only just succeeded, and the realm was full of dread.

sentences.zh: 此與太寧火同事。

translations.literal: This was the same matter as the Taining fire.
translations.idiomatic: This matched the Taining fire in meaning.

sentences.zh: 晉孝武帝太元十年正月，立國子學。

translations.literal: In the first month of the tenth year of Taiyuan under Emperor Xiaowu of Jin, the Imperial University was established.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the tenth Taiyuan year under Emperor Xiaowu of Jin, the Imperial University was founded.

sentences.zh: 學生多頑嚚，因風放火，焚房百餘間。

translations.literal: The students were mostly stubborn and stupid; taking advantage of the wind they set fires and burned more than a hundred rooms.
translations.idiomatic: Many students were obstinate and unruly; they used the wind to set fires and burned more than a hundred rooms.

sentences.zh: 是後考課不厲，賞黜無章，有育才之名，無收賢之實。

translations.literal: Afterward examinations were not strict, rewards and dismissals lacked standards; there was the name of nurturing talent but not the reality of gathering the worthy.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward examinations grew lax, promotions and dismissals followed no rule, and though the state claimed to nurture talent it gathered no worthy men.

sentences.zh: 書云：「知人則哲。

translations.literal: The Documents say: "To know men is to be wise."
translations.idiomatic: The Documents say, "To know men is wisdom."

sentences.zh: 」此不哲之罰先兆也。

translations.literal: " This was the foretoken of the penalty for lack of wisdom.
translations.idiomatic: " This was the first sign of the penalty for want of discernment.

sentences.zh: 太元十三年十二月乙未，延賢堂災。

translations.literal: On the yiwei day of the twelfth month of the thirteenth year of Taiyuan, the Yanxian Hall burned.
translations.idiomatic: On the yiwei day of the twelfth month of the thirteenth Taiyuan year, fire destroyed the Yanxian Hall.

sentences.zh: 丙申，螽斯、則百堂及客館、驃騎庫皆災。

translations.literal: On the bingshen day, the Zhongsi Hall, the Zebo Hall, the guest quarters, and the Rapid Cavalry armory all burned.
translations.idiomatic: On the bingshen day fire also destroyed the Zhongsi Hall, the Zebo Hall, the guest quarters, and the Rapid Cavalry storehouse.

sentences.zh: 于時朝多弊政，衰陵日兆。

translations.literal: At that time the court had many corrupt policies, and decline daily showed its signs.
translations.idiomatic: The court was rife with corrupt government, and decline grew daily more plain.

sentences.zh: 不哲之罰，皆有象類。

translations.literal: The penalties for lack of wisdom all had their symbolic types.
translations.idiomatic: Each penalty for want of discernment had its symbolic counterpart.

sentences.zh: 主相不悟，終至亂亡云。

translations.literal: The ruler and chancellor did not understand, and in the end came disorder and ruin—or so it is said.
translations.idiomatic: Ruler and chief minister failed to understand, and in the end the realm fell into chaos and ruin.

sentences.zh: 晉安帝隆安二年三月，龍舟二乘災。

translations.literal: In the third month of the second year of Long'an under Emperor An of Jin, two dragon boats burned.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the second Long'an year under Emperor An of Jin, two imperial dragon boats burned.

sentences.zh: 是水沴火也。

translations.literal: This was water harming fire.
translations.idiomatic: Water was afflicting fire.

sentences.zh: 晉安帝元興元年八月庚子，尚書下舍曹火。

translations.literal: On the gengzi day of the eighth month of the first year of Yuanxing under Emperor An of Jin, fire broke out in the lower quarters bureau of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: On the gengzi day of the eighth month of the first Yuanxing year under Emperor An of Jin, fire destroyed the lower quarters bureau of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 元興三年，盧循攻略廣州，刺史吳隱之閉城固守。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yuanxing, Lu Xun attacked and seized Guangzhou; the inspector Wu Yinshi shut the city and held firm.
translations.idiomatic: In the third Yuanxing year Lu Xun besieged Guangzhou, and Inspector Wu Yinshi closed the walls and defended the city.

sentences.zh: 是年十月壬戌夜，大火起。

translations.literal: On the night of the renxu day of the tenth month of that year, a great fire broke out.
translations.idiomatic: On the night of the renxu day of the tenth month that year a great fire broke out.

sentences.zh: 時民人避寇，盈滿城內。

translations.literal: At the time the people were fleeing the bandits and filled the city to overflowing.
translations.idiomatic: The people had fled the raiders and packed the city wall to wall.

sentences.zh: 隱之懼有應賊，但務嚴兵，不先救火，由是府舍焚燒蕩盡，死者萬餘人，因遂散潰，悉為賊擒。

translations.literal: Yinshi feared there were collaborators with the bandits and devoted himself only to strict military measures, not first fighting the fire; thereby the government offices were burned clean away, more than ten thousand people died, the defenders then scattered in rout, and all were seized by the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Yinshi, fearing traitors within, devoted himself only to tightening the guard and did not fight the fire first; the government quarter was burned to the ground, more than ten thousand died, the defenders broke and fled, and all were taken by the enemy.

sentences.zh: 殆與襄陽火同占也。

translations.literal: This was nearly the same prognostication as the fire at Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: The omen closely matched that of the Xiangyang fire.

sentences.zh: 晉安帝義熙四年七月丁酉，尚書殿中吏部曹火。

translations.literal: On the dingyou day of the seventh month of the fourth year of Yixi under Emperor An of Jin, fire broke out in the Palace Secretariat's Personnel Bureau within the Hall.
translations.idiomatic: On the dingyou day of the seventh month of the fourth Yixi year under Emperor An of Jin, fire destroyed the Personnel Bureau of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 義熙十一年，京都所在大行火災，吳界尤甚。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Yixi, wherever one went in the capital region there were great fire disasters, especially severe in the Wu territories.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh Yixi year fires raged throughout the capital region, worst of all in Wu.

sentences.zh: 火防甚峻，猶自不絕。

translations.literal: Fire precautions were very strict, yet the fires still did not cease.
translations.idiomatic: Fire precautions were severe, yet the blazes would not stop.

sentences.zh: 王弘時為吳郡，白日在聽事上，見天上有一赤物下，狀如信幡，徑集路南人家屋上，火即復大發。

translations.literal: Wang Hong was then governor of Wu Commandery; in broad daylight in the audience hall he saw a red object descend from the sky, shaped like a signal banner, which went straight to the roof of a house south of the road, and the fire immediately broke out again on a great scale.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Hong was then governor of Wu; in broad daylight at court he saw a red object descend from heaven like a signal banner, settle on a rooftop south of the road, and at once a great fire flared up again.

sentences.zh: 弘知天為之災，不罪火主。

translations.literal: Hong knew Heaven had sent this disaster and did not punish the householder where the fire started.
translations.idiomatic: Hong knew Heaven had sent the calamity and did not blame the household where the fire began.

sentences.zh: 宋文帝元嘉五年正月戊子，京邑大火。

translations.literal: On the wuzi day of the first month of the fifth year of Yuanjia under Emperor Wen of Song, a great fire broke out in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: On the wuzi day of the first month of the fifth Yuanjia year under Emperor Wen of Song, the capital burned.

sentences.zh: 元嘉七年十二月乙亥，京邑火，延燒太社北牆。

translations.literal: On the yihai day of the twelfth month of the seventh year of Yuanjia, the capital burned, spreading to the northern wall of the Grand Altar of Soil and Grain.
translations.idiomatic: On the yihai day of the twelfth month of the seventh Yuanjia year fire struck the capital and reached the northern wall of the Grand Altar of Soil and Grain.

sentences.zh: 元嘉二十九年三月壬午，京邑大火，風雷甚壯。

translations.literal: On the renwu day of the third month of the twenty-ninth year of Yuanjia, a great fire broke out in the capital; wind and thunder were very fierce.
translations.idiomatic: On the renwu day of the third month of the twenty-ninth Yuanjia year the capital burned amid violent wind and thunder.

sentences.zh: 後廢帝元徽三年正月己巳，京邑大火。

translations.literal: On the jisi day of the first month of the third year of Yuanhui under the Deposed Emperor, a great fire broke out in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: On the jisi day of the first month of the third Yuanhui year under the Deposed Emperor, the capital burned.

sentences.zh: 元徽三年二月戊辰，京邑大火，燒二岸數千家。

translations.literal: On the wuchen day of the second month of the third year of Yuanhui, a great fire broke out in the capital, burning several thousand households on both banks.
translations.idiomatic: On the wuchen day of the second month of the third Yuanhui year the capital burned, destroying thousands of homes on both riverbanks.

sentences.zh: 恒燠

translations.literal: Constant heat
translations.idiomatic: Constant Heat

sentences.zh: 庶徵之恒燠，劉向、班固以冬亡冰及霜不殺草應之。

translations.literal: Among the various signs, constant heat—Liu Xiang and Ban Gu took winter without ice and frost that does not kill grass as its response.
translations.idiomatic: Of the various portents, constant heat—Liu Xiang and Ban Gu interpreted winters without ice and frosts that failed to kill grass as its manifestation.

sentences.zh: 京房易傳又曰：「夏則暑殺人，冬則物華實。」

translations.literal: Jing Fang's Tradition of the Changes also says: "In summer, heat kills people; in winter, things flower and bear fruit."
translations.idiomatic: Jing Fang's Yi tradition also says, "In summer heat kills men; in winter plants bloom and fruit."

sentences.zh: 吳孫亮建興元年九月，桃李華。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the first year of Jianxing under Sun Liang of Wu, peach and plum trees blossomed.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of the first Jianxing year under Sun Liang of Wu, peach and plum trees flowered out of season.

sentences.zh: 孫權世，政煩賦重，民彫於役。

translations.literal: In Sun Quan's age, government was vexatious and taxes heavy; the people were worn down by corvée.
translations.idiomatic: Under Sun Quan government was burdensome and taxes heavy, and the people were exhausted by forced labor.

sentences.zh: 是時諸葛恪始輔政，息校官，原逋責，除關梁，崇寬厚。

translations.literal: At that time Zhuge Ke had just begun to assist in government, suspending school officials, remitting overdue debts, abolishing frontier tolls, and honoring leniency and generosity.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Zhuge Ke had just taken power, suspended school inspections, remitted overdue taxes, abolished frontier tolls, and promoted leniency.

sentences.zh: 此舒緩之應也。

translations.literal: This was the response of easing and relaxation.
translations.idiomatic: This answered the easing of government.

sentences.zh: 一說桃李寒華為草妖，或屬華孽。

translations.literal: One view holds that peach and plum blossoming in cold weather is a grass prodigy, or perhaps belongs among flower calamities.
translations.idiomatic: Some hold that peach and plum flowering in cold weather is a grass prodigy, or a floral calamity.

sentences.zh: 魏元帝景元三年十月，桃李華。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the third year of Jingyuan under Emperor Yuan of Wei, peach and plum trees blossomed.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of the third Jingyuan year under Emperor Yuan of Wei, peach and plum trees flowered out of season.

sentences.zh: 自高貴弒死之後，晉文王深樹恩德，事崇優緩，此其應也。

translations.literal: After the assassination of the Gaogui emperor, the Prince of Jin deeply planted favor and virtue and honored leniency and ease in affairs—this was the response.
translations.idiomatic: After the regicide of the Gaogui emperor, the Prince of Jin cultivated benevolence and eased government—this was the omen's fulfillment.

sentences.zh: 晉穆帝永和九年十二月，桃李華。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of the ninth year of Yonghe under Emperor Mu of Jin, peach and plum trees blossomed.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of the ninth Yonghe year under Emperor Mu of Jin, peach and plum trees flowered out of season.

sentences.zh: 是時簡文輔政，事多弛略，舒緩之應也。

translations.literal: At that time Emperor Jianwen assisted in government; affairs were mostly lax and neglected—the response of easing and relaxation.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Emperor Jianwen governed; affairs were lax and neglected—the omen of easing answered.

sentences.zh: 宋順帝昇明元年十月，於潛桃、李、柰結實。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the first year of Shengming under Emperor Shun of Song, in Yuqian peach, plum, and pear trees bore fruit.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of the first Shengming year under Emperor Shun of Song, peach, plum, and pear trees in Yuqian bore fruit out of season.

sentences.zh: 草妖

translations.literal: Grass prodigies
translations.idiomatic: Grass Prodigies

sentences.zh: 漢獻帝建安二十五春正月，魏武帝在洛陽，將起建始殿，伐濯龍祠樹而血出；

translations.literal: In the first month of spring of the twenty-fifth year of Jian'an under Emperor Xian of Han, the Martial Emperor of Wei was in Luoyang, about to raise the Jianshi Hall; he cut trees at the Zhuolong Shrine and blood flowed out;
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of spring of the twenty-fifth Jian'an year under Emperor Xian of Han, the Martial Emperor of Wei was in Luoyang preparing to build the Jianshi Hall; when he felled trees at the Zhuolong Shrine, blood gushed forth;

sentences.zh: 又掘徙棃，根傷亦血出。

translations.literal: he also dug up and moved pear trees, and when the roots were injured blood also flowed out.
translations.idiomatic: when he uprooted pear trees to transplant them, blood flowed from the wounded roots as well.

sentences.zh: 帝惡之，遂寢疾，是月崩。

translations.literal: The emperor regarded this with loathing, then took to his bed with illness, and that month he died.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor took this as an evil omen, fell ill, and died that month.

sentences.zh: 蓋草妖，又赤祥也。

translations.literal: This was probably a grass prodigy, and also a red portent.
translations.idiomatic: This was a grass prodigy and also a red omen.

sentences.zh: 是歲，魏文帝黃初元年也。

translations.literal: That year was the first year of Huangchu under Emperor Wen of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: That year was the first Huangchu year of Emperor Wen of Wei.

sentences.zh: 吳孫亮五鳳元年六月，交趾稗草化為稻。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the first year of Wufeng under Sun Liang of Wu, barnyard grass in Jiaozhi transformed into rice.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the first Wufeng year under Sun Liang of Wu, barnyard grass in Jiaozhi turned into rice.

sentences.zh: 昔三苗將亡，五穀變種。

translations.literal: In antiquity when the Three Miao were about to perish, the five grains changed their kinds.
translations.idiomatic: When the Three Miao were about to fall, the five grains changed their kinds.

sentences.zh: 此草妖也。

translations.literal: This was a grass prodigy.
translations.idiomatic: It was an omen among grass prodigies.

sentences.zh: 其後亮廢。

translations.literal: Afterward Liang was deposed.
translations.idiomatic: Later Liang was deposed.

sentences.zh: 蜀劉禪景耀五年，宮中大樹無故自折。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Jingyao under Liu Shan of Shu, a great tree in the palace broke of itself without cause.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth Jingyao year under Liu Shan of Shu, a great tree in the palace snapped for no apparent reason.

sentences.zh: 譙周憂之，無所與之言，乃書柱曰：「眾而大，其之會，具而授，若何復。

translations.literal: Qiao Zhou was troubled by it; having no one with whom to speak of it, he wrote on a pillar: "Many and great, they will meet; complete and bestowed—how can there be restoration?"
translations.idiomatic: Qiao Zhou was troubled but spoke to no one; instead he wrote on a pillar, "Many and great, they shall meet; complete and bestowed—how can there be restoration?"

sentences.zh: 」言曹者眾也；

translations.literal: " He meant that Cao means "many";
translations.idiomatic: " By this he meant that Cao means "many";

sentences.zh: 魏者大也；

translations.literal: Wei means "great";
translations.idiomatic: Wei means "great";

sentences.zh: 眾而大，天下其當會也；

translations.literal: many and great—the realm will surely be united;
translations.idiomatic: many and great—the realm will be united;

sentences.zh: 具而授，如何復有立者乎。

translations.literal: complete and bestowed—how can there again be one who stands?
translations.idiomatic: complete and bestowed—how can Shu stand again?

sentences.zh: 蜀果亡，如周言。

translations.literal: Shu indeed perished, just as Zhou had said.
translations.idiomatic: Shu did fall, exactly as Zhou had predicted.

sentences.zh: 此草妖也。

translations.literal: This too was a grass prodigy.
translations.idiomatic: This too was counted among grass prodigies.

sentences.zh: 吳孫晧天璽元年，吳郡臨平湖自漢末穢塞，是時一夕忽開除無草。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tianxi under Sun Hao of Wu, Linping Lake in Wu Commandery had been foully blocked since the end of Han; at this time in one night it suddenly opened clear with no weeds.
translations.idiomatic: In the first Tianxi year under Sun Hao of Wu, Linping Lake in Wu Commandery, blocked and foul since late Han, opened in a single night, clear of weeds.

sentences.zh: 長老相傳，此湖塞，天下亂，此湖開，天下平。

translations.literal: The elders handed down the saying: when this lake is blocked, the realm is in disorder; when this lake opens, the realm is at peace.
translations.idiomatic: Elders said that when the lake was blocked the realm fell into chaos, and when it opened the realm would be at peace.

sentences.zh: 吳尋亡，而九服為一。

translations.literal: Wu was soon destroyed, and the nine domains became one.
translations.idiomatic: Wu soon fell, and the nine domains were united under one rule.

sentences.zh: 吳孫晧天紀三年八月，建業有鬼目菜生工黃狗家，依緣棗樹，長丈餘，莖廣四寸，厚三分。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the third year of Tianji under Sun Hao of Wu, in Jianye a guimu vegetable grew at the home of the artisan Huang Gou, clinging to a jujube tree; it was more than a zhang long, its stem four inches wide and three fen thick.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of the third Tianji year under Sun Hao of Wu, a guimu plant grew at the home of the artisan Huang Gou in Jianye, climbing a jujube tree to more than a zhang in height, with a stem four inches across and three fen thick.

sentences.zh: 又有蕒菜生工吳平家，高四尺，如枇杷形，上圓徑一尺八寸，下莖廣五寸，兩邊生葉緣色。

translations.literal: There was also a qi vegetable growing at the home of the artisan Wu Ping, four chi high, shaped like a loquat; the upper round part was one chi eight inches in diameter, the lower stem five inches wide, with green leaves growing on both sides.
translations.idiomatic: A qi plant also grew at the home of the artisan Wu Ping, four chi tall and loquat-shaped, with a round crown one chi eight inches across, a stem five inches wide below, and green leaves on both sides.

sentences.zh: 東觀案圖，名鬼目作芝草，蕒菜作平慮。

translations.literal: The Eastern Observatory checked its charts and named the guimu as zhi grass and the qi vegetable as pinglu.
translations.idiomatic: The Eastern Observatory consulted its charts and read the guimu as zhi grass and the qi plant as pinglu.

sentences.zh: 遂以狗為侍芝郎，平為平慮郎，皆銀印青綬。

translations.literal: Gou was therefore made Attendant Zhi Gentleman and Ping was made Pinglu Gentleman, both with silver seals and blue cords.
translations.idiomatic: Gou was made Attendant Zhi Gentleman and Ping Pinglu Gentleman, each with a silver seal and blue cord.

sentences.zh: 干寶曰：「明年晉平吳，王濬止船，正得平渚，姓名顯然，指事之徵也。

translations.literal: Gan Bao said: "The next year Jin pacified Wu; Wang Jun moored his boats precisely at Pingzhu—the names were manifestly clear; this was a sign pointing to the event."
translations.idiomatic: Gan Bao wrote, "The next year Jin conquered Wu; Wang Jun moored his fleet at Pingzhu—the names were unmistakable, a sign pointing straight at the event."

sentences.zh: 黃狗者，吳以土運承漢，故初有黃龍之瑞，及其季年，而有鬼目之妖，託黃狗之家，黃稱不改，而貴賤大殊。

translations.literal: Huang Gou: Wu, taking the element earth to succeed Han, at first had the auspicious sign of the yellow dragon; in its final years came the guimu prodigy, lodged in the house of Huang Gou—the yellow designation unchanged, yet noble and base greatly altered.
translations.idiomatic: As for Huang Gou: Wu, inheriting Han through the element earth, had once received the yellow dragon as an auspicious sign; in its last years the guimu prodigy appeared in the house of Huang Gou—the yellow name remained, but fortune and ruin were utterly reversed.

sentences.zh: 天道精微之應也。」

translations.literal: This was the subtle response of Heaven's Way."
translations.idiomatic: Such was the subtle response of Heaven's Way."

sentences.zh: 晉惠帝元康二年春，巴西郡界竹生花，紫色，結實如麥，外皮青，中赤白，味甘。

translations.literal: In spring of the second year of Yuankang under Emperor Hui of Jin, within the borders of Baxi Commandery bamboo produced flowers, purple in color, bearing fruit like wheat; the outer skin was green, the interior red-white, and sweet in taste.
translations.idiomatic: In spring of the second Yuankang year under Emperor Hui of Jin, bamboo in Baxi Commandery flowered purple and bore fruit like wheat, green-skinned and red-white within, sweet to the taste.

sentences.zh: 元康九年六月庚子，有桑生東宮西廂，日長尺餘；

translations.literal: On the gengzi day of the sixth month of the ninth year of Yuankang, a mulberry tree grew in the western wing of the Eastern Palace, growing more than a chi a day;
translations.idiomatic: On the gengzi day of the sixth month of the ninth Yuankang year a mulberry sprouted in the western wing of the Eastern Palace and grew more than a chi a day;

sentences.zh: 甲辰，枯死。

translations.literal: on the jiachen day it withered and died.
translations.idiomatic: by the jiachen day it had withered away.

sentences.zh: 此與殷太戊同妖。

translations.literal: This was the same prodigy as under Emperor Taiwu of Yin.
translations.idiomatic: This matched the prodigy of Emperor Taiwu of Yin.

sentences.zh: 太子不能悟，故至廢戮也。

translations.literal: The crown prince could not understand, and therefore came to deposition and execution.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince failed to understand, and was deposed and killed.

sentences.zh: 班固稱「野木生朝而暴長，小人將暴居大臣之位，危亡國家，象朝將為墟也」。

translations.literal: Ban Gu said: "When wild trees grow in the court and shoot up violently, petty men will violently occupy the positions of great ministers, endangering and destroying the state—the court will become a ruin."
translations.idiomatic: Ban Gu wrote, "When wild trees spring up in the court and grow violently, petty men will seize the posts of great ministers, endanger the state, and the court itself will become a ruin."

sentences.zh: 是後孫秀、張林尋用事，遂至大亂。

translations.literal: Afterward Sun Xiu and Zhang Lin soon held power, and great disorder followed.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward Sun Xiu and Zhang Lin soon seized power, and the realm fell into great chaos.

sentences.zh: 晉惠帝永康元年四月丁巳，立皇孫臧為皇太孫。

translations.literal: On the dingsi day of the fourth month of the first year of Yongkang under Emperor Hui of Jin, the emperor's grandson Zang was established as imperial great-grandson heir.
translations.idiomatic: On the dingsi day of the fourth month of the first Yongkang year under Emperor Hui of Jin, the emperor's grandson Zang was named imperial great-grandson heir.

sentences.zh: 五月甲子，就東宮。

translations.literal: On the jiazi day of the fifth month he took up residence in the Eastern Palace.
translations.idiomatic: On the jiazi day of the fifth month he entered the Eastern Palace.

sentences.zh: 桑又生於西廂。

translations.literal: A mulberry tree again grew in the western wing.
translations.idiomatic: Another mulberry sprouted in the western wing.

sentences.zh: 明年，趙倫篡位，鴆殺臧。

translations.literal: The next year Zhao Lun usurped the throne and poisoned Zang to death.
translations.idiomatic: The next year Zhao Lun seized the throne and poisoned Zang.

sentences.zh: 此與愍懷同妖也。

translations.literal: This was the same prodigy as with Prince Minhuai.
translations.idiomatic: This was the same prodigy as that of Prince Minhuai.

sentences.zh: 永康元年四月，壯武國有桑化為柏。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the first year of Yongkang, in Zhuangwu Principality a mulberry tree transformed into a cypress.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the first Yongkang year a mulberry in Zhuangwu Principality turned into a cypress.

sentences.zh: 是月，張華遇害。

translations.literal: That month, Zhang Hua met with murder.
translations.idiomatic: That month Zhang Hua was killed.

sentences.zh: 晉孝懷帝永嘉三年冬，項縣桑樹有聲如解材，民謂之桑林哭。

translations.literal: In the winter of the third year of Yongjia under Emperor Huai of Jin, mulberry trees in Xiang County made sounds like splitting timber, and the people called it the Weeping Mulberry Grove.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the third Yongjia year under Emperor Huai of Jin, mulberry trees in Xiang County made sounds like splitting lumber, and the people called it "the weeping mulberry grove."

sentences.zh: 案劉向說，桑者喪也，又為哭聲，不祥之甚。

translations.literal: According to Liu Xiang's tradition, sang (mulberry) means sang (mourning), and also signifies weeping sounds—most inauspicious.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xiang's tradition holds that sang (mulberry) homophonically means sang (mourning) and also evokes wailing—a deeply inauspicious omen.

sentences.zh: 是時京師虛弱，胡寇交逼，司馬越無衞上國之心，四年冬，委而南出，至五年春，薨于此城，石勒邀其眾，圍而射之，王公以下至庶人，死者十餘萬人，又剖越棺焚其尸。

translations.literal: At that time the capital was enfeebled, barbarian raiders pressed from all sides, and Sima Yue had no heart to defend the realm; in the winter of the fourth year he abandoned it and marched south; by spring of the fifth year he died at that fortress; Shi Le intercepted his host, surrounded and shot them; from kings and dukes down to common people more than a hundred thousand died; and Yue's coffin was opened and his corpse burned.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the capital was weak and barbarian invaders pressed in from every side; Sima Yue had no will to defend the state. In the winter of the fourth year he abandoned the capital and fled south; by spring of the fifth year he died at that city. Shi Le ambushed his army, besieged and shot them, and more than a hundred thousand nobles and commoners died; Yue's coffin was opened and his corpse burned.

sentences.zh: 是敗也，中原無所請命，洛京尋沒。

translations.literal: With this defeat none in the Central Plains had a place to seek orders; Luoyang soon fell.
translations.idiomatic: After this defeat no authority remained in the Central Plains, and Luoyang soon fell.

sentences.zh: 桑哭之應也。

translations.literal: This was the response of the weeping mulberries.
translations.idiomatic: This fulfilled the omen of the weeping mulberries.

sentences.zh: 永嘉六年五月，無錫縣有四株茱萸樹，相樛而生，狀若連理。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the sixth year of Yongjia, in Wuxi County four cornel trees grew entwined together, their appearance like joined trunks.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the sixth Yongjia year four cornel trees in Wuxi County grew intertwined, resembling joined trunks.

sentences.zh: 先是，郭景純筮延陵偃鼠，遇臨之益，曰：「後當復有妖樹生，若瑞而非，辛螫之木也。

translations.literal: Earlier, Guo Jingchun divined for Yanling's recumbent rat and obtained Lin changing to Yi; he said: "Later an uncanny tree will again appear; though seeming auspicious it is not—the wood of pungent stinging."
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Guo Jingchun (Guo Pu) divined for Yanling's recumbent rat and obtained the hexagram Lin changing to Yi, saying: "An ominous tree will appear again—seemingly auspicious but not the wood of the pungent cornel."

sentences.zh: 儻有此，東南數百里必有作逆者。

translations.literal: If this should occur, within several hundred li to the southeast there will surely be one who rises in rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: If such a tree appears, rebellion will arise within several hundred li to the southeast.

sentences.zh: 」其後徐馥作亂。

translations.literal: " Afterwards Xu Fu raised rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: " Soon afterward Xu Fu rebelled.

sentences.zh: 此草妖也，郭以為木不曲直。

translations.literal: This was a grass prodigy; Guo took it as wood not upright and straight.
translations.idiomatic: This was a grass prodigy; Guo Pu regarded it as wood that would not stand upright and straight.

sentences.zh: 永嘉六年七月，豫章郡有樟樹久枯，是月忽更榮茂。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the sixth year of Yongjia, in Yuzhang Commandery a camphor tree long withered suddenly flourished lushly that month.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the sixth Yongjia year a camphor tree in Yuzhang Commandery that had long been withered suddenly flourished again.

sentences.zh: 與昌邑枯社復生同占。

translations.literal: It shares the same omen-reading as the withered altar of Changyi reviving.
translations.idiomatic: It carries the same omen as the revival of Changyi's withered altar tree.

sentences.zh: 懷帝不終其祚，元帝由支族興之應也。

translations.literal: Emperor Huai not completing his reign, and Emperor Yuan rising from a collateral line—the response thereof.
translations.idiomatic: It foretold that Emperor Huai would not reign to term and that Emperor Yuan would rise from a collateral line.

sentences.zh: 晉明帝太寧元年九月，會稽剡縣木生如人面。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the first year of Taining under Emperor Ming of Jin, in Shanyin County of Kuaiji wood grew in the likeness of a human face.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of the first Taining year under Emperor Ming of Jin, wood in Shanyin County, Kuaiji, grew shaped like a human face.

sentences.zh: 是後王敦稱兵作逆，禍敗無成。

translations.literal: After this Wang Dun raised troops in rebellion; disaster and defeat brought no success.
translations.idiomatic: Later Wang Dun raised an army in rebellion but met disaster and failed.

sentences.zh: 漢哀、靈之世，並有此妖，而人貌備具，故其禍亦大。

translations.literal: In the ages of Emperors Ai and Ling of Han there were both this prodigy, but with the human form complete in every feature, hence their calamities were also great.
translations.idiomatic: The reigns of Emperors Ai and Ling of Han had similar prodigies, but with full human features—hence far greater calamities.

sentences.zh: 今此但人面而已，故其變亦輕。

translations.literal: Now this was only a human face; hence its transformation was also slight.
translations.idiomatic: Here there was only a face, so the omen was comparatively mild.

sentences.zh: 晉成帝咸和六年五月癸亥，曲阿有柳樹倒地六載，是月忽復起生。

translations.literal: On the guihai day of the fifth month of the sixth year of Xianhe under Emperor Cheng of Jin, in Qu'e a willow that had lain fallen six years suddenly revived and grew that month.
translations.idiomatic: On the guihai day of the fifth month of the sixth Xianhe year a willow in Qu'e that had lain fallen for six years suddenly sprang back to life.

sentences.zh: 咸和九年五月甲戌，吳雄家有死榆樹，是日因風雨起生。

translations.literal: On the jiaxu day of the fifth month of the ninth year of Xianhe, at the home of Wu Xiong there was a dead elm tree that because of wind and rain revived and grew that day.
translations.idiomatic: On the jiaxu day of the fifth month of the ninth Xianhe year a dead elm at Wu Xiong's house revived in a windstorm.

sentences.zh: 與漢上林斷柳起生同象。

translations.literal: It shared the same image as the severed willow reviving in the Han Shanglin Park.
translations.idiomatic: It matched the omen of the severed willow that revived in Han's Shanglin Park.

sentences.zh: 初，康帝為吳王，于時雖改封琅邪，而猶食吳郡為邑。

translations.literal: At first Emperor Kang was Prince of Wu; at the time although re-enfeoffed as Prince of Langye, he still took Wu Commandery as his fief.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Kang had first been Prince of Wu; though later re-enfeoffed as Prince of Langye, he still drew his fief income from Wu Commandery.

sentences.zh: 是帝越正體饗國之象也。

translations.literal: This was the image of the emperor surpassing the proper body to receive the realm.
translations.idiomatic: This symbolized the emperor ascending beyond his proper line to inherit the realm.

sentences.zh: 曲阿先亦吳地，象見吳邑雄舍，又天意也。

translations.literal: Qu'e too had formerly been Wu territory; the image appeared at the house of Xiong in Wu domain—again Heaven's intent.
translations.idiomatic: Qu'e had also been Wu territory; the omen appeared at Xiong's home in Wu—again Heaven's design.

sentences.zh: 晉哀帝興寧三年五月癸卯，盧陵西昌縣脩明家有死栗樹，是日忽起生。

translations.literal: On the guimao day of the fifth month of the third year of Xingning under Emperor Ai of Jin, at the home of Xiuming in Xichang County of Luling a dead chestnut tree suddenly revived and grew that day.
translations.idiomatic: On the guimao day of the fifth month of the third Xingning year a dead chestnut at Xiuming's home in Xichang County, Luling, suddenly sprang back to life.

sentences.zh: 時孝武年四歲，而簡文居蕃，四海宅心。

translations.literal: At the time Emperor Xiaowu was four years old, while Emperor Jianwen held the feudatory and all within the seas fixed their hearts on him.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Emperor Xiaowu was four and Emperor Jianwen held the princely fief; all the realm looked to him.

sentences.zh: 及得位垂統，則祚隆孝武。

translations.literal: When he obtained the throne and passed down the lineage, the reign then honored Xiaowu.
translations.idiomatic: When he took the throne and established the succession, the line passed to Emperor Xiaowu.

sentences.zh: 識者竊曰西昌脩明之祥，帝諱實應之矣。

translations.literal: Those who understood privately said the auspice of Xichang Xiuming truly answered to the emperor's taboo name.
translations.idiomatic: Observers murmured that the omen at Xichang-Xiuming matched the emperor's taboo name.

sentences.zh: 是與漢宣帝頗同象也。

translations.literal: This rather shared the same image as Emperor Xuan of Han.
translations.idiomatic: The omen closely resembled that of Emperor Xuan of Han.

sentences.zh: 晉海西太和元年，涼州楊樹生松。

translations.literal: In the first year of Taihe under Emperor Fei of Jin, in Liang Province poplars bore pine.
translations.idiomatic: In the first Taihe year under Emperor Fei of Jin poplars in Liang Province sprouted pine.

sentences.zh: 天戒若曰，松不改柯易葉，楊者柔脆之木，此永久之業，將集危亡之地。

translations.literal: Heaven's warning seems to say: pine does not change its branches and alter its leaves; poplar is a soft and brittle wood—this enduring enterprise will gather upon ground of peril and ruin.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven's warning seems to say: pine keeps its branches and leaves unchanged, while poplar is soft and brittle—enduring rule would settle in a place of peril and collapse.

sentences.zh: 是後張天錫降氐。

translations.literal: After this Zhang Tianshi surrendered to the Di.
translations.idiomatic: Later Zhang Tianshi surrendered to the Di.

sentences.zh: 晉孝武太元十四年六月，建寧同樂縣枯木斷折，忽然自立相屬。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the fourteenth year of Taiyuan under Emperor Xiaowu of Jin, in Tongle County of Jianning withered trees broke and snapped, then suddenly stood upright and joined together.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the fourteenth Taiyuan year withered trees in Tongle County, Jianning, snapped apart and then suddenly stood upright, rejoined.

sentences.zh: 京房易傳曰：「棄正作淫，厥妖木斷自屬。

translations.literal: The Yizhuan of Jing Fang says: "Abandoning the upright and acting licentiously—the prodigy is wood broken yet joining itself."
translations.idiomatic: Jing Fang's Changes commentary says: "When the upright is cast aside and licentiousness reigns, the prodigy is broken wood rejoining itself."

sentences.zh: 妃后有專，木仆反立。

translations.literal: When consorts and empresses hold exclusive power, trees fall and rise again.
translations.idiomatic: When consorts and empresses dominate, fallen trees stand upright again.

sentences.zh: 」是時治道方僻，多失其正。

translations.literal: " At that time the way of governance was just turning deviant; much lost its proper course.
translations.idiomatic: " At the time government had turned corrupt and much had lost its proper bearing.

sentences.zh: 其後張夫人專寵，及帝崩，兆庶歸咎張氏焉。

translations.literal: After this Lady Zhang held exclusive favor; when the emperor died the myriad people laid blame on the Zhang clan.
translations.idiomatic: Later Lady Zhang monopolized the emperor's favor; when he died the people blamed the Zhang family.

sentences.zh: 晉安帝元興三年，荊、江二界生竹實如麥。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yuanxing under Emperor An of Jin, on the border of Jing and Jiang bamboo bore fruit like wheat.
translations.idiomatic: In the third Yuanxing year under Emperor An of Jin bamboo on the Jing-Jiang border bore grain-like fruit.

sentences.zh: 晉安帝義熙二年九月，揚州營揚武將軍營士陳蓋家有苦蕒菜，莖高四尺六寸，廣三尺二寸。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the second year of Yixi under Emperor An of Jin, at the home of Chen Gai, a soldier in the Yangzhou camp of the General Who Establishes Martiality, a bitter amaranth plant had a stalk four feet six inches high and three feet two inches broad.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of the second Yixi year a bitter amaranth at soldier Chen Gai's home in the Yangzhou camp of the General Who Establishes Martiality stood four feet six inches tall with a spread three feet two inches wide.

sentences.zh: 此殆與吳終同象也。

translations.literal: This perhaps shared the same image as the end of Wu.
translations.idiomatic: This likely foreshadowed the fall of Wu—the same omen, the same pattern.

sentences.zh: 義熙中，宮城上御道左右皆生蒺蔾。

translations.literal: During Yixi, on the palace city wall to both sides of the imperial roadway tribulus grew.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yixi era tribulus sprouted along both sides of the imperial road atop the palace walls.

sentences.zh: 草妖也。

translations.literal: A grass prodigy.
translations.idiomatic: It was a grass prodigy.

sentences.zh: 蒺蔾有刺，不可踐而行，生宮牆及馳道，天戒若曰，人君拱默不能聽政，雖居宸極，猶若空宮，雖有御道，未嘗馳騁，皆生蒺蔾若空廢也。

translations.literal: Tribulus has thorns and cannot be trodden and walked upon; growing on palace walls and the imperial race road, Heaven's warning seems to say: the ruler folds his hands in silence and cannot hear governance; though dwelling at the apex of the palace he is as if in an empty hall; though having an imperial road he has never galloped—all grow tribulus as if abandoned and void.
translations.idiomatic: Tribulus is thorny and impassable; growing on palace walls and the imperial road, Heaven's warning seems to say: the ruler sits mute and does not govern; though enthroned he is as in an empty palace; though an imperial road exists he never rides—tribulus covers all as if the court were abandoned.

sentences.zh: 義熙八年，太社生薰樹于壇側。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Yixi, at the Grand Altar of Earth a xun tree grew beside the mound.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth Yixi year a xun tree sprouted beside the mound at the Grand Altar of Earth.

sentences.zh: 薰於文尚黑，宋水德將王之符也。

translations.literal: Xun in writing favors black; the token that Song's Water virtue is about to become king.
translations.idiomatic: The character xun favors black in writing—a sign that Song, whose element is Water, was destined to take the throne.

sentences.zh: 羽蟲之孽

translations.literal: Calamities of feathered creatures
translations.idiomatic: Feathered Creature Calamities

sentences.zh: 魏文帝黃初四年五月，有鵜鵠鳥集靈芝池。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the fourth year of Huangchu under Emperor Wen of Wei, pelican birds gathered at the Lingzhi Pool.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the fourth Huangchu year pelicans gathered at the Lingzhi Pool.

sentences.zh: 案劉向說，此羽蟲之孽，又青祥也。

translations.literal: According to Liu Xiang's tradition, this was a calamity of feathered creatures, and also a green portent.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xiang's tradition classifies this as a feathered-creature calamity and also a green omen.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「此詩人所謂汙澤者也。

translations.literal: An edict said: "This is what the poets call the defiled marsh."
translations.idiomatic: An edict declared: "This is what the poets call the fouled marsh."

sentences.zh: 曹詩刺恭公遠君子，近小人。

translations.literal: The Cao ode satirizes Duke Gong for keeping distant from gentlemen and drawing near to petty men.
translations.idiomatic: A Cao ode rebukes Duke Gong for spurning worthy men and favoring flatterers.

sentences.zh: 今豈有賢智之士，處于下位，否則斯鳥胡為而至哉？

translations.literal: Now are there perhaps worthy and wise men occupying low stations? Otherwise why would this bird come?
translations.idiomatic: Are worthy men languishing in low office—or why else would this bird appear?

sentences.zh: 其博舉天下儁德茂才，獨行君子，以答曹人之刺。

translations.literal: Let there broadly be raised throughout the realm men of preeminent virtue and abundant talent, and upright gentlemen of singular conduct, to answer the satire of the Cao men.
translations.idiomatic: Let the court broadly seek men of outstanding virtue, abundant talent, and upright character to answer the ode's rebuke.

sentences.zh: 」於是楊彪、管寧之徒，咸見薦舉。

translations.literal: " Thereupon men such as Yang Biao and Guan Ning were all recommended and elevated.
translations.idiomatic: " Thereupon Yang Biao, Guan Ning, and others were all recommended.

sentences.zh: 此謂覩妖知懼者也。

translations.literal: This is what is called seeing a prodigy and knowing fear.
translations.idiomatic: Here was a ruler who saw an omen and took warning.

sentences.zh: 雖然不能優容亮直，而多溺偏私矣。

translations.literal: Even so he could not generously accommodate openness and uprightness, but mostly indulged partial favoritism.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he could not truly tolerate the frank and upright, and still favored his intimates.

sentences.zh: 京房易傳曰：「辟退有德，厥妖水鳥集于國井。」

translations.literal: The Yizhuan of Jing Fang says: "Repelling and dismissing the virtuous—the prodigy is water birds gathering at the state well."
translations.idiomatic: Jing Fang's Changes commentary says: "When the worthy are driven away, water birds gather at the royal well."

sentences.zh: 黃初末，宮中有鷰生鷹，口爪俱赤。

translations.literal: At the end of Huangchu, in the palace a swallow bore a hawk; beak and claws alike were red.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Huangchu a swallow in the palace hatched a hawk with red beak and claws.

sentences.zh: 此與商紂、宋隱同象。

translations.literal: This shared the same image as King Zhou of Shang and Duke Yin of Song.
translations.idiomatic: It matched omens from the reigns of King Zhou of Shang and Duke Yin of Song.

sentences.zh: 景初元年，又有鷰生鉅鷇於衞國涓桃里李蓋家。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jingchu, again a swallow bore a great fledgling at the home of Li Gai in Juantao Ward of Weiguo.
translations.idiomatic: In the first Jingchu year another swallow hatched a huge fledgling at Li Gai's home in Juantao Ward, Wei Commandery.

sentences.zh: 形若鷹，吻似燕。

translations.literal: Its form resembled a hawk; its bill resembled a swallow.
translations.idiomatic: It looked like a hawk but had a swallow's bill.

sentences.zh: 案劉向說，此羽蟲之孽，又赤眚也。

translations.literal: According to Liu Xiang's tradition, this was a calamity of feathered creatures, and also a red disaster.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xiang's tradition classifies this as a feathered-creature calamity and also a red omen.

sentences.zh: 高堂隆曰：「此魏室之大異，宜防鷹揚之臣於蕭牆之內。

translations.literal: Gao Tanglong said: "This is a great prodigy for the house of Wei; one ought to guard against hawk-rising ministers within the inner court."
translations.idiomatic: Gao Tanglong said: "This is a grave portent for Wei; beware hawk-like ministers within the palace walls."

sentences.zh: 」其後晉宣王起，遂有魏室。

translations.literal: " After this the Prince of Jin rose, and thus possessed the house of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: " Later the Prince of Jin rose and seized Wei.

sentences.zh: 漢獻帝建安二十三年，禿鶖鳥集鄴宮文昌殿後池。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year of Jian'an under Emperor Xian of Han, bald storks gathered at the rear pool of the Wenchang Hall in Ye's palace.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-third Jian'an year bald storks gathered at the pool behind Wenchang Hall in Ye Palace.

sentences.zh: 明年，魏武王薨。

translations.literal: The next year the Martial King of Wei died.
translations.idiomatic: The following year the Martial King of Wei passed away.

sentences.zh: 魏文帝黃初三年，又集雒陽芳林園池。

translations.literal: In the third year of Huangchu under Emperor Wen of Wei, they again gathered at the pool of Fanglin Garden in Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the third Huangchu year they gathered again at the Fanglin Garden pool in Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 七年，又集。

translations.literal: In the seventh year they gathered again.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year they appeared again.

sentences.zh: 其夏，文帝崩。

translations.literal: That summer Emperor Wen died.
translations.idiomatic: That summer Emperor Wen passed away.

sentences.zh: 景初末，又集芳林園池。
