translations.literal: At the end of Jingchu they again gathered at the Fanglin Garden pool.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Jingchu they gathered once more at the Fanglin Garden pool.

sentences.zh: 前世再至，輒有大喪，帝惡之。

translations.literal: In earlier ages when they came twice there was always great mourning; the emperor loathed this.
translations.idiomatic: Twice before their appearance had foretold imperial death, and the emperor dreaded it.

sentences.zh: 其年，明帝崩。

translations.literal: That year Emperor Ming died.
translations.idiomatic: That year Emperor Ming passed away.

sentences.zh: 蜀劉禪建興九年十月，江陽至江州有鳥從江南飛渡江北，不能達，墮水死者以千餘。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the ninth year of Jianxing under Liu Shan of Shu, from Jiangyang to Jiangzhou birds flew from south of the Yangtze to cross to north of the river; unable to reach it, more than a thousand fell into the water and died.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of the ninth Jianxing year birds flying north from south of the Yangtze between Jiangyang and Jiangzhou failed to cross; more than a thousand drowned.

sentences.zh: 是時諸葛亮連年動眾，志吞中夏，而終死渭南，所圖不遂。

translations.literal: At that time Zhuge Liang for years mobilized armies, intent on swallowing the Central Xia, yet finally died at Weinan; what he plotted was not achieved.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Zhuge Liang had campaigned year after year to conquer the Central Plains but died at Weinan with his ambitions unfulfilled.

sentences.zh: 又諸將分爭，頗喪徒旅。

translations.literal: Moreover the various generals contended in division, and fairly lost soldiers and followers.
translations.idiomatic: Generals also quarreled among themselves, losing many troops.

sentences.zh: 鳥北飛不能達，墮水死，皆有其象也。

translations.literal: Birds flying north unable to reach it, falling into water and dying—all had their corresponding images.
translations.idiomatic: Birds flying north and drowning in the river—all had their symbolic meaning.

sentences.zh: 亮竟不能過渭，又其應乎。

translations.literal: Liang in the end could not cross the Wei River—is this again the response?
translations.idiomatic: Liang never crossed the Wei—is this the omen fulfilled?

sentences.zh: 此與漢、楚國烏鬭墮泗水觕類矣。

translations.literal: This was roughly of the same kind as the Han and Chu states' crows battling and falling into the Si River.
translations.idiomatic: This resembled the omen when Han and Chu crows fought and fell into the Si River.

sentences.zh: 魏明帝青龍三年，戴鵀巢鉅鹿人張臶家。

translations.literal: In the third year of Qinglong under Emperor Ming of Wei, hoopoes nested at the home of Zhang Jie of Julu.
translations.idiomatic: In the third Qinglong year hoopoes nested at the home of Zhang Jie in Julu.

sentences.zh: 臶博學有高節，不應袁紹、高幹之命，魏太祖辟亦不至，優游嘉遁，門徒數百，太守王肅雅敬焉。

translations.literal: Jie was broad in learning and of lofty integrity; he did not respond to the summons of Yuan Shao or Gao Gan, nor did he come when the Martial Emperor of Wei summoned him; he roamed at ease in gracious retirement, with disciples numbering in the hundreds; Prefect Wang Su honored him with elegant respect.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jie was a learned recluse of lofty integrity who refused summons from Yuan Shao and Gao Gan and ignored the Martial Emperor's invitation; he lived in gracious retirement with hundreds of disciples, and Prefect Wang Su held him in high esteem.

sentences.zh: 時年百餘歲，謂門人曰：「戴鵀陽鳥，而巢于門陰，此凶祥也。

translations.literal: At the time over a hundred years old, he told his disciples: "The hoopoe is a yang bird, yet it nests in the yin of the gate—this is ominous auspice."
translations.idiomatic: Then over a hundred years old, he told his disciples: "The hoopoe is a yang bird, yet it nests in the shadow of my gate—this is a dire omen."

sentences.zh: 」乃援琴歌詠，作詩一首，旬日而卒。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he took up the zither and sang in verse, composed one poem, and within ten days died.
translations.idiomatic: " He played the zither and sang, composed a poem, and died within ten days.

sentences.zh: 按占，羽蟲之孽也。

translations.literal: According to divinatory reckoning, this was a calamity of feathered creatures.
translations.idiomatic: By omen-reading it was a feathered-creature calamity.

sentences.zh: 魏明帝景初元年，陵霄閣始構，有鵲巢其上。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jingchu under Emperor Ming of Wei, as the Lingxiao Pavilion was first being built, a magpie nested upon it.
translations.idiomatic: In the first Jingchu year, as Lingxiao Pavilion was first under construction, a magpie nested on it.

sentences.zh: 鵲體白黑雜色。

translations.literal: The magpie's body was mixed white and black in color.
translations.idiomatic: The magpie was mottled black and white.

sentences.zh: 此羽蟲之孽，又白黑祥也。

translations.literal: This was a calamity of feathered creatures, and also a white-and-black portent.
translations.idiomatic: It was a feathered-creature calamity and also a black-and-white omen.

sentences.zh: 帝以問高堂隆，對曰：「詩云：『惟鵲有巢，惟鳩居之。

translations.literal: The emperor questioned Gao Tanglong; he replied: "The Odes say: 'Only the magpie has a nest; only the dove dwells in it.'"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked Gao Tanglong, who replied: "The Odes say: 'The magpie makes the nest, but the turtledove lives in it.'"

sentences.zh: 』今興起宮室，而鵲來巢，此宮室未成，身不得居之之象。

translations.literal: " Now raising palace halls, yet the magpie comes to nest—this is the image of palace halls not yet completed and the person not able to dwell in them.
translations.idiomatic: " The palace is still rising, yet a magpie nests there—the image of unfinished halls whose builder will never inhabit them."

sentences.zh: 天意若曰，宮室未成，將有它姓制御之，不可不深慮。

translations.literal: Heaven's intent seems to say: palace halls not yet completed—another surname will control them; one cannot fail to reflect deeply.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven seems to warn: the halls will not be finished before another clan takes control—this demands deep reflection.

sentences.zh: 」於是帝改容動色。

translations.literal: " Thereupon the emperor changed his countenance and showed emotion.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor's expression changed.

sentences.zh: 吳孫權赤烏十二年四月，有兩烏銜鵲墮東館。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the twelfth year of Chiwu under Sun Quan of Wu, two crows carrying a magpie fell at the Eastern Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the twelfth Chiwu year two crows dropped a magpie they were carrying at the Eastern Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 權使領丞相朱據燎鵲以祭。

translations.literal: Quan sent Director of Affairs Grand Chancellor Zhu Ju to burn the magpie as a sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan had Grand Chancellor Zhu Ju burn the magpie as an offering.

sentences.zh: 案劉歆說，此羽蟲之孽，又黑祥也。

translations.literal: According to Liu Xin's tradition, this was a calamity of feathered creatures, and also a black portent.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xin's tradition classifies this as a feathered-creature calamity and also a black omen.

sentences.zh: 視不明，聽不聰之罰也。

translations.literal: It is the penalty for vision not clear and hearing not keen.
translations.idiomatic: It was punishment for blindness and deafness in governance.

sentences.zh: 是時權意溢德衰，信讒好殺，二子將危，將相俱殆。

translations.literal: At that time Quan's intent overflowed and virtue declined; he trusted slander and loved killing; the two princes were about to be imperiled; generals and ministers alike were endangered.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Sun Quan's judgment failed and his virtue waned; he trusted slander and favored executions; both heirs were in peril and his ministers endangered.

sentences.zh: 覩妖不悟，加之以燎，昧道之甚者也。

translations.literal: Seeing a prodigy yet not comprehending, and moreover adding burning to it—most deluded in the Way.
translations.idiomatic: He saw the omen yet understood nothing, and burned the bird besides—a profound blindness to the Way.

sentences.zh: 明年，太子和廢，魯王霸賜死，朱據左遷，陸議憂卒，是其應也。

translations.literal: The next year Crown Prince He was deposed, Prince of Lu Ba was granted death, Zhu Ju was transferred leftward, Lu Yi died of grief—all this was the response.
translations.idiomatic: The next year Crown Prince He was deposed, Prince Ba of Lu was ordered to die, Zhu Ju was demoted, and Lu Yi died of grief—the omen fulfilled.

sentences.zh: 東館，典教之府，鵲墮東館，又天意乎。

translations.literal: The Eastern Pavilion is the office of canonical teaching; the magpie falling at the Eastern Pavilion—is this again Heaven's intent?
translations.idiomatic: The Eastern Pavilion housed the crown prince's educators—the magpie's fall there was surely Heaven's warning again.

sentences.zh: 吳孫權太元二年正月，封前太子和為南陽王，遣之長沙。

translations.literal: In the first month of the second year of Taiyuan under Sun Quan of Wu, the former Crown Prince He was enfeoffed as Prince of Nanyang and sent to Changsha.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the second Taiyuan year the former Crown Prince He was made Prince of Nanyang and sent to Changsha.

sentences.zh: 有鵲巢其帆檣。

translations.literal: A magpie nested on its sail and mast.
translations.idiomatic: A magpie nested on the ship's mast and rigging.

sentences.zh: 和故宮僚聞之，皆憂慘，以為檣末傾危，非久安之象。

translations.literal: He's former palace staff hearing this were all grieved and distressed, taking the tip of the mast as leaning and perilous—not an image of long peace.
translations.idiomatic: He's former retainers heard of it and were deeply troubled, taking a nest at the masthead as an omen of imminent collapse—not long stability.

sentences.zh: 是後果不得其死。

translations.literal: After this he indeed did not obtain death in due course.
translations.idiomatic: In the end he did not die a natural death.

sentences.zh: 吳孫亮建興二年十一月，大鳥五見于春申。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of the second year of Jianxing under Sun Liang of Wu, five great birds appeared at Chunshen.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of the second Jianxing year under Sun Liang of Wu, five large birds appeared at Chunshen.

sentences.zh: 吳人以為鳳皇，明年，改元為五鳳。

translations.literal: The people of Wu took them for the phoenix; the next year the reign title was changed to Wufeng.
translations.idiomatic: Wu took them for phoenixes and the following year renamed the era Wufeng, "Five Phoenixes."

sentences.zh: 漢桓帝時，有五色大鳥。

translations.literal: In the time of Emperor Huan of Han, there was a five-colored great bird.
translations.idiomatic: During Emperor Huan's reign a great bird of five colors appeared.

sentences.zh: 司馬彪云：「政治衰缺，無以致鳳，乃羽蟲孽耳。

translations.literal: Sima Biao said: "Government decline and deficiency—there is no way to bring forth the phoenix; it is merely a calamity of feathered creatures.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Biao wrote: "When governance fails, phoenixes do not come; such birds are feathered-creature calamities, nothing more.

sentences.zh: 」孫亮未有德政，孫峻驕暴方甚，此與桓帝同事也。

translations.literal: " Sun Liang had not yet had virtuous governance, and Sun Jun's arrogant violence was then at its height—this is the same matter as with Emperor Huan.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Liang had shown no virtuous rule, and Sun Jun's tyranny was at its height—the same pattern as under Emperor Huan.

sentences.zh: 案瑞應圖，大鳥似鳳而為孽者非一，疑皆是也。

translations.literal: According to the Chart of Auspicious Responses, great birds resembling the phoenix yet becoming calamities are not one alone; I suspect all are such.
translations.idiomatic: The Chart of Auspicious Responses lists many great birds that resemble phoenixes yet signify calamity; likely all these cases belong in that category.

sentences.zh: 吳孫晧建衡三年，西苑言鳳皇集，以之改元。

translations.literal: In the third year of Jianheng under Sun Hao of Wu, the Western Park reported phoenixes gathering; on this basis the reign title was changed.
translations.idiomatic: In the third Jianheng year Sun Hao of Wu heard that phoenixes had gathered in the Western Park and renamed the era accordingly.

sentences.zh: 義同於亮。

translations.literal: The meaning is the same as with Liang.
translations.idiomatic: The import was the same as in Sun Liang's case.

sentences.zh: 晉武帝泰始四年八月，翟雉飛上閶闔門。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the fourth year of Taishi under Emperor Wu of Jin, pheasants flew up onto the Changhe Gate.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of the fourth Taishi year pheasants flew up to the Changhe Gate.

sentences.zh: 趙倫既篡，洛陽得異鳥，莫能名。

translations.literal: After Zhao Lun had usurped the throne, Luoyang obtained a strange bird that no one could name.
translations.idiomatic: Once Zhao Lun had seized the throne, an unidentifiable strange bird appeared in Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 倫使人持出，周旋城邑匝以問人。

translations.literal: Lun sent a man to carry it out and circle the city in full, asking people.
translations.idiomatic: Lun had the bird carried through the city in circuits, asking everyone what it was.

sentences.zh: 積日，宮西有小兒見之，逆自言曰：「服留鳥翳。

translations.literal: After many days, west of the palace a small child saw it and of himself said contrary: "A fuliu bird obscures.
translations.idiomatic: After days without an answer, a boy west of the palace saw the bird and called out of his own accord: "It is a fuliu bird—

sentences.zh: 」持者即還白倫。

translations.literal: " The carrier at once returned and reported to Lun.
translations.idiomatic: The bearer immediately went back and told Lun.

sentences.zh: 倫使更求小兒。

translations.literal: Lun sent men to seek the child again.
translations.idiomatic: Lun sent men to find the boy again.

sentences.zh: 至，又見之，將入宮，密籠鳥，閉兒戶中。

translations.literal: When he arrived and saw it again, as he was about to enter the palace, they secretly caged the bird and shut the child in a room.
translations.idiomatic: When the boy came and saw the bird again, just as he was entering the palace they caged the bird in secret and locked him in a room.

sentences.zh: 明日視，悉不見。

translations.literal: The next day they looked—all were gone.
translations.idiomatic: The next morning bird and boy had both vanished.

sentences.zh: 此羽蟲之孽，又妖之甚者也。

translations.literal: This is a calamity of feathered creatures, and moreover among the gravest of prodigies.
translations.idiomatic: This was a feathered-creature calamity and one of the most ominous prodigies.

sentences.zh: 趙倫篡位，有鶉入太極殿，雉集東堂。

translations.literal: When Zhao Lun usurped the throne, a quail entered the Hall of Supreme Polarity, and pheasants gathered at the Eastern Hall.
translations.idiomatic: At Zhao Lun's usurpation a quail entered the Hall of Supreme Polarity and pheasants roosted at the Eastern Hall.

sentences.zh: 按太極、東堂，皆朝享聽政之所，而鶉、雉同日集之者，天意若曰，不當居此位也。

translations.literal: The Hall of Supreme Polarity and the Eastern Hall are both places for court audience and hearing government; that quail and pheasants gathered there on the same day—Heaven's intent seems to say, one ought not occupy this position.
translations.idiomatic: Both halls were seats of audience and rule; quail and pheasant appearing there together on the same day read as Heaven's verdict that Lun had no right to the throne.

sentences.zh: 詩云「鵲之疆疆，鶉之奔奔。

translations.literal: The Classic of Poetry says: "The magpies dart dart, the quails run run.
translations.idiomatic: The Odes say: "Magpies wheel and quarrel, quails rush and flutter—

sentences.zh: 人之無良，我以為君」。

translations.literal: People without goodness—I take them for lords."
translations.idiomatic: yet to men without virtue we still bow as lords."

sentences.zh: 其此之謂乎。

translations.literal: Is this not what is meant?
translations.idiomatic: Was the Odes not speaking of just such a man?

sentences.zh: 昔殷宗感雉雊，懼而修德，倫覩二物，曾不知戒，故至滅亡也。

translations.literal: Formerly the Ancestor of Yin was moved by a pheasant's crow, feared and cultivated virtue; Lun saw the two creatures yet never knew warning—hence he reached destruction.
translations.idiomatic: Long ago King Wu Ding of Yin heard a pheasant crow, took fright, and reformed his conduct; Lun saw two such omens yet took no warning—and perished.

sentences.zh: 晉孝懷帝永嘉元年二月，洛陽東北步廣里地陷，有鵝出，蒼色者飛翔沖天，白者止焉。

translations.literal: In the second month of the first year of Yongjia under Emperor Huai of Jin, the ground sank at Buguang Lane northeast of Luoyang; geese emerged—the dark-colored ones flew soaring to the sky, the white ones halted there.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the first Yongjia year the ground collapsed at Buguang Lane northeast of Luoyang and geese emerged; the dark birds soared skyward while the white ones remained below.

sentences.zh: 此羽蟲之孽，又黑白祥也。

translations.literal: This is a calamity of feathered creatures, and also an omen of black and white.
translations.idiomatic: This was a feathered-creature calamity and also an omen of black and white.

sentences.zh: 董養曰：「步廣，周之狄泉，盟會地也。

translations.literal: Dong Yang said: "Buguang—Zhou's Diquan, a place of league meetings.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Yang commented: "Buguang was Diquan of Zhou, where feudal lords once met in alliance.

sentences.zh: 白者金色，蒼為胡象，其可盡言乎。

translations.literal: White is the color of metal; dark is the image of the barbarians—can it all be spoken?
translations.idiomatic: White is the color of Jin, dark the hue of the barbarians—need more be said?

sentences.zh: 」是後劉淵、石勒相繼擅華，懷、愍二帝淪滅非所。

translations.literal: " After this Liu Yuan and Shi Le in succession seized control of the Central Land; Emperors Huai and Min perished in places not their own.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward Liu Yuan and Shi Le seized the heartland in turn, and Emperors Huai and Min died far from their capitals.

sentences.zh: 晉孝懷帝世，周玘家有鵝在籠中，而頭斷籠外。

translations.literal: In the reign of Emperor Huai of Jin, in Zhou Qi's household a goose was in a cage yet its head was severed outside the cage.
translations.idiomatic: During Emperor Huai's reign Zhou Qi kept a goose in a cage whose head was cut off outside the bars.

sentences.zh: 玘亡後家誅。

translations.literal: After Qi's death his household was executed.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhou Qi died his entire family was put to death.

sentences.zh: 晉明帝太寧三年八月庚戌，有鳥二，蒼黑色，翼廣一丈四尺。

translations.literal: On gengxu day of the eighth month of the third year of Taining under Emperor Ming of Jin, there were two birds, dark black, with wings fourteen feet in span.
translations.idiomatic: On gengxu day in the eighth month of the third Taining year two dark black birds appeared, each with a wingspan of fourteen feet.

sentences.zh: 其一集司徒府，射而殺之；

translations.literal: One settled at the Chancellor's office and was shot and killed;
translations.idiomatic: One alighted on the Chancellor's gate and was shot dead;

sentences.zh: 其一集市北家人舍，亦獲焉。

translations.literal: one settled at a commoner's house north of the market and was also captured.
translations.idiomatic: the other landed at a house north of the market and was captured as well.

sentences.zh: 此羽蟲之孽，又黑祥也。

translations.literal: This is a calamity of feathered creatures, and also a black portent.
translations.idiomatic: This was a feathered-creature calamity and also a black omen.

sentences.zh: 閏月戊子，帝崩。

translations.literal: On wuzi day of the intercalary month, the Emperor died.
translations.idiomatic: On wuzi day in the intercalary month the Emperor died.

sentences.zh: 後有蘇峻、祖約之亂。

translations.literal: Afterward came the rebellions of Su Jun and Zu Yue.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after came the revolts of Su Jun and Zu Yue.

sentences.zh: 晉成帝咸和二年正月，有五鷗鳥集殿庭。

translations.literal: In the first month of the second year of Xianhe under Emperor Cheng of Jin, five gulls gathered in the palace courtyard.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the second Xianhe year five gulls gathered in the palace courtyard.

sentences.zh: 此又白祥也。

translations.literal: This is again a white portent.
translations.idiomatic: This too was a white omen.

sentences.zh: 是時庾亮苟違眾謀，將召蘇峻，有言不從之咎，故白祥先見也。

translations.literal: At that time Yu Liang perversely went against the counsel of the multitude and was about to summon Su Jun—there is the fault of words not heeded; hence the white portent appeared first.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Liang had ignored general counsel and was about to recall Su Jun—a fault of disregarding sound advice—so the white omen appeared beforehand.

sentences.zh: 三年二月，峻果作亂，宮室焚毀，化為汙萊，其應也。

translations.literal: In the second month of the third year, Jun indeed rebelled; palace halls were burned and destroyed, turned to filthy wasteland—this was the response.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the third year Su Jun rebelled as foretold; the palace was burned to ruin, the fulfillment of the omen.

sentences.zh: 晉成帝咸康八年七月，白鷺集殿屋。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the eighth year of Xiankang under Emperor Cheng of Jin, white egrets gathered on the palace roof.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the eighth Xiankang year white egrets roosted on the palace roof.

sentences.zh: 是時康帝始即位，此不永之祥也。

translations.literal: At that time Emperor Kang had just acceded—this is an omen of not long enduring.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Kang had just taken the throne—a sign that his reign would not last.

sentences.zh: 後涉再朞而帝崩。

translations.literal: Later spanning two cycles, the Emperor died.
translations.idiomatic: Within two years the Emperor was dead.

sentences.zh: 劉向曰：「野鳥入處，宮室將空。

translations.literal: Liu Xiang said: "When wild birds enter and dwell, the palace chambers will be emptied.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xiang wrote: "When wild birds enter the palace, the halls will stand empty.

sentences.zh: 」張瓘在涼州正朝，放隹雀諸鳥，出手便死；

translations.literal: " Zhang Guan was at the morning audience in Liangzhou; when he released pheasants and various birds, they died as soon as they left his hand;
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Guan held court in Liangzhou; when he released pheasants and other birds, they died the moment they left his hand,

sentences.zh: 左右放者悉飛去。

translations.literal: those released by his attendants all flew away.
translations.idiomatic: but those released by his attendants all flew off unharmed.

sentences.zh: 晉孝武帝太元十六年正月，鵲巢太極東頭鴟尾，又巢國子學堂西頭。

translations.literal: In the first month of the sixteenth year of Taiyuan under Emperor Xiaowu of Jin, magpies nested on the owl-tail finial at the east end of the Supreme Hall, and also nested at the west end of the National University hall.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the sixteenth Taiyuan year magpies nested on the eastern owl-tail of the Supreme Hall and on the western end of the National University hall.

sentences.zh: 十八年，東宮始成，十九年正月，鵲又巢其西門。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year the Eastern Palace was first completed; in the first month of the nineteenth year, magpies again nested at its western gate.
translations.idiomatic: The Eastern Palace was completed in the eighteenth year; in the first month of the nineteenth magpies nested at its western gate as well.

sentences.zh: 此殆與魏景初同占。

translations.literal: This is probably the same divination as in Jingchu of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: This likely carried the same meaning as the Jingchu omen in Wei.

sentences.zh: 學堂，風教所聚；

translations.literal: The academy hall is where wind and teaching gather;
translations.idiomatic: The academy is where culture and instruction are centered;

sentences.zh: 西門，金行之祥也。

translations.literal: the western gate is an omen of the Metal phase.
translations.idiomatic: the western gate bears an omen associated with the Metal phase.

sentences.zh: 晉安帝義熙三年，龍驤將軍朱猗戍壽陽。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yixi under Emperor An of Jin, General of Dragon Might Zhu Yi garrisoned Shouyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the third Yixi year General Zhu Yi of Dragon Might garrisoned Shouyang.

sentences.zh: 婢炊飯，忽有羣烏集竈，競來啄噉，婢驅逐不去。

translations.literal: A maidservant was cooking rice when suddenly a flock of crows gathered on the stove, competing to come peck and eat; the maid drove them but they would not leave.
translations.idiomatic: While a maid was cooking, crows suddenly swarmed the stove and fought over the food; she shooed them but they would not go.

sentences.zh: 有獵狗咋殺烏鵲，餘者因共啄狗即死，又噉其肉，唯餘骨存。

translations.literal: A hunting dog bit and killed a crow or magpie; the rest together pecked the dog and it immediately died; they also ate its flesh, only bones remaining.
translations.idiomatic: A hunting dog killed one crow; the rest turned on the dog, pecked it dead, and devoured its flesh until only bones remained.

sentences.zh: 五年六月，猗死。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the fifth year, Yi died.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the fifth year Zhu Yi died.

sentences.zh: 宋武帝永初三年，臨軒拜徐羨之為司空，百僚陪位，有二野鸛集太極鴟尾鳴呼。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yongchu under Emperor Wu of Song, at the throne facing to invest Xu Xianzhi as Minister of Works, with the hundred officials in attendance, two wild storks gathered on the owl-tail of the Supreme Hall, calling out.
translations.idiomatic: In the third Yongchu year, as Emperor Wu invested Xu Xianzhi as Minister of Works with the court in attendance, two wild storks perched on the Supreme Hall's owl-tail and cried out.

sentences.zh: 少帝景平二年春，鸛巢太廟西鴟尾，驅去復還。

translations.literal: In the spring of the second year of Jingping under the Lesser Emperor, storks nested on the western owl-tail of the Imperial Ancestral Temple; driven away, they returned.
translations.idiomatic: In the second Jingping spring storks nested on the western owl-tail of the Imperial Ancestral Temple; driven off, they returned.

sentences.zh: 文帝元嘉二年春，有江鷗鳥數百，集太極殿前小階內。

translations.literal: In the spring of the second year of Yuanjia under Emperor Wen, several hundred river gulls gathered within the small steps before the Hall of Supreme Polarity.
translations.idiomatic: In the second Yuanjia spring hundreds of river gulls gathered on the lower terrace before the Supreme Hall.

sentences.zh: 明年，誅徐羨之等。

translations.literal: The next year, Xu Xianzhi and others were executed.
translations.idiomatic: The following year Xu Xianzhi and his allies were put to death.

sentences.zh: 羊禍

translations.literal: Sheep calamities
translations.idiomatic: Sheep Calamities

sentences.zh: 晉成帝咸和二年五月，司徒王導廄，羊生無後足。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the second year of Xianhe under Emperor Cheng of Jin, in Chancellor Wang Dao's stable a lamb was born without hind feet.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the second Xianhe year a lamb without hind legs was born in Chancellor Wang Dao's stable.

sentences.zh: 此羊禍也。

translations.literal: This is a sheep calamity.
translations.idiomatic: This was a sheep calamity.

sentences.zh: 京房易傳曰：「足少者，下不勝任也。

translations.literal: The Yijing Tradition of Jing Fang says: "When feet are lacking, those below cannot bear the burden.
translations.idiomatic: Jing Fang's Tradition of Changes says: "Missing feet mean subordinates cannot sustain their duties."

sentences.zh: 」明年，蘇峻入京都，導與成帝俱幽石頭，僅乃免身。

translations.literal: " The next year Su Jun entered the capital; Dao and Emperor Cheng were both confined at Shitou, barely escaping with their lives.
translations.idiomatic: The next year Su Jun seized the capital; Wang Dao and Emperor Cheng were imprisoned at Shitou and barely survived.

sentences.zh: 是其應也。

translations.literal: This was the response.
translations.idiomatic: The omen was fulfilled.

sentences.zh: 宋孝武帝大明七年，永平郡獻三角羊。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Daming under Emperor Xiaowu of Song, Yongping commandery presented a three-horned sheep.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh Daming year Yongping commandery presented a sheep with three horns.

sentences.zh: 羊禍也。

translations.literal: A sheep calamity.
translations.idiomatic: This too was a sheep calamity.

sentences.zh: 赤眚赤祥

translations.literal: Red blights and red portents
translations.idiomatic: Red Blights and Red Portents

sentences.zh: 公孫淵時，襄平北市生肉，長圍各數尺，有頭目口喙，無手足，而動搖。

translations.literal: In the time of Gongsun Yuan, at the north market of Xiangping flesh grew, long and round each several feet, with head, eyes, mouth, and beak, without hands or feet, yet swaying.
translations.idiomatic: During Gongsun Yuan's reign flesh several feet long sprouted in Xiangping's north market, shaped like heads with eyes and beaks but no limbs, yet quivering.

sentences.zh: 此赤眚也。

translations.literal: This is a red blight.
translations.idiomatic: This was a red blight.

sentences.zh: 占曰：「有形不成，有體無聲，其國滅亡。

translations.literal: Divination says: "Form without completion, body without sound—the state will perish.
translations.idiomatic: The oracle reads: "Shape without wholeness, body without voice—the kingdom will fall."

sentences.zh: 」淵尋為魏所誅。

translations.literal: " Yuan was soon executed by Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan was soon destroyed by Wei.

sentences.zh: 吳戍將鄧嘉殺猪祠神，治畢縣之，忽見一人頭往食肉，嘉引弓射中之，咋咋作聲，繞屋三日。

translations.literal: Wu garrison general Deng Jia killed a pig to sacrifice to the spirit; when the preparation was finished and hung up, suddenly a human head appeared going to eat the meat; Jia drew his bow and shot it; it made chattering sounds, circling the house for three days.
translations.idiomatic: Wu garrison commander Deng Jia sacrificed a pig to a spirit and hung the meat to cure; a human head appeared and devoured it. Jia shot it with an arrow; it chattered and circled his house for three days.

sentences.zh: 近赤祥也。

translations.literal: This approximates a red portent.
translations.idiomatic: This was akin to a red omen.

sentences.zh: 後人白嘉謀北叛，闔門被誅。

translations.literal: Later someone reported that Jia plotted to rebel northward; his whole household was executed.
translations.idiomatic: Later someone accused Jia of plotting to defect north; his entire family was executed.

sentences.zh: 京房易妖曰：「山見葆，江于邑，邑有兵，狀如人頭赤色。」

translations.literal: Jing Fang's Changes on Prodigies says: "On the mountain appears bao; the river at the town—the town has soldiers, in form like a human head, red in color."
translations.idiomatic: Jing Fang's Book of Change Prodigies says: "Mountains show strange growth, rivers flood the town; the town will know war—shaped like a human head, red in hue."

sentences.zh: 吳諸葛恪將見誅，盥洗水血臭；

translations.literal: When Zhuge Ke of Wu was about to be executed, the hand-washing water smelled of blood;
translations.idiomatic: As Zhuge Ke of Wu awaited execution, his wash water reeked of blood;

sentences.zh: 侍者授衣，衣亦臭。

translations.literal: when attendants handed him clothes, the clothes too smelled foul.
translations.idiomatic: and the robes his attendants brought likewise stank.

sentences.zh: 此近赤祥也。

translations.literal: This approximates a red portent.
translations.idiomatic: These were red omens of the same kind.

sentences.zh: 晉武帝太康七年十一月，河陰有赤雪二頃。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of the seventh year of Taikang under Emperor Wu of Jin, at Heyin there was red snow covering two qing.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of the seventh Taikang year red snow covered two qing at Heyin.

sentences.zh: 此赤祥也。

translations.literal: This is a red portent.
translations.idiomatic: This was a red omen.

sentences.zh: 後涉四載而帝崩，王宮遂亂。

translations.literal: Later spanning four years the Emperor died, and the royal palace was thrown into disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Four years later the Emperor died and the palace fell into chaos.

sentences.zh: 晉惠帝元康五年三月，呂縣有流血，東西百餘步。

translations.literal: In the third month of the fifth year of Yuankang under Emperor Hui of Jin, in Lyu County there was flowing blood, east to west over a hundred-odd paces.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the fifth Yuankang year blood flowed across more than a hundred paces in Lyu County.

sentences.zh: 此赤祥也。

translations.literal: This is a red portent.
translations.idiomatic: This was a red omen.

sentences.zh: 元康末，窮凶極亂，僵尸流血之應也。

translations.literal: At the end of Yuankang, extreme wickedness and utmost disorder—this was the response of corpses lying strewn and blood flowing.
translations.idiomatic: At Yuankang's close came utter wickedness and chaos—the omen of corpses and flowing blood fulfilled.

sentences.zh: 干寶以為後八載而封雲亂徐州，殺傷數萬人，是其應也。

translations.literal: Gan Bao considered that eight years later Feng Yun raised rebellion in Xuzhou, killing and wounding tens of thousands—this was the response.
translations.idiomatic: Gan Bao held that eight years later Feng Yun's rebellion in Xuzhou killed tens of thousands—the omen's fulfillment.

sentences.zh: 晉惠帝永康元年三月，尉氏雨血。

translations.literal: In the third month of the first year of Yongkang under Emperor Hui of Jin, at Weishi blood rained from the sky.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the first Yongkang year blood rain fell at Weishi.

sentences.zh: 夫政刑舒緩，則有常燠赤祥之妖。

translations.literal: When government and punishments are lax and slow, there are prodigies of constant heat and red portents.
translations.idiomatic: Lax governance and delayed justice breed prodigies of unnatural warmth and red omens.

sentences.zh: 此歲正月，送愍懷太子幽于許宮。

translations.literal: In the first month of this year, the Crown Prince Minhuai was sent to be confined at Xu Palace.
translations.idiomatic: That same year, in the first month, Crown Prince Minhuai was imprisoned at the palace in Xu.

sentences.zh: 天戒若曰，不宜緩恣姦人，將使太子冤死。

translations.literal: Heaven's admonition seems to say: one ought not be lax and indulge wicked men—it will cause the crown prince to die unjustly.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven seemed to warn: do not indulge villains so lightly, lest the crown prince die unjustly.

sentences.zh: 惠帝愚眊不悟，是月愍懷遂斃。

translations.literal: Emperor Hui was dull and dim and did not comprehend; that month Minhuai then died.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Hui was too dull to understand; that month Minhuai was dead.

sentences.zh: 於是王室釁成，禍流天下。

translations.literal: Thereupon the royal house's rift was formed, and calamity flowed throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: The breach in the imperial house was opened and disaster spread across the land.

sentences.zh: 淖齒殺齊閔王日，天雨血沾衣，天以告也，此之謂乎。

translations.literal: On the day Nao Chi killed King Min of Qi, Heaven rained blood staining clothes—Heaven thereby announced; is this what is meant?
translations.idiomatic: When Nao Chi killed King Min of Qi, blood rain stained men's robes—Heaven's proclamation. Was this the same sign?

sentences.zh: 京房易傳曰：「歸獄不解，茲謂追非，厥咎天雨血，茲謂不親，民有怨心，不出三年，無其宗人。

translations.literal: The Yijing Tradition of Jing Fang says: "Prisoners returned but not released—this is called pursuing wrong; its penalty is blood rain from Heaven; this is called not being close—the people have resentful hearts; within three years there will be none of his clansmen.
translations.idiomatic: Jing Fang's Tradition of Changes states: "When prisoners are not released, it is called pursuing error; the penalty is blood rain from Heaven. When the ruler is distant from his people, resentment grows; within three years none of his kin will remain."

sentences.zh: 」又曰：「佞人祿，功臣戮，天雨血。」

translations.literal: " It also says: "When flatterers receive salary and meritorious ministers are slaughtered, Heaven rains blood."
translations.idiomatic: It also says: "When sycophants prosper and worthy ministers are killed, blood rains from the sky."

sentences.zh: 晉愍帝建興四年十二月丙寅，丞相府斬督運令史淳于伯，血逆流上柱二丈三尺。

translations.literal: On bingyin day of the twelfth month of the fourth year of Jianxing under Emperor Min of Jin, at the Chancellor's office Transport Supervisor Clerk Chunyu Bo was beheaded; blood flowed upward against the pillar twenty-three feet.
translations.idiomatic: On bingyin day in the twelfth month of the fourth Jianxing year the Chancellor's office executed Transport Clerk Chunyu Bo; his blood flowed up a pillar twenty-three feet high.

sentences.zh: 此赤祥也。

translations.literal: This is a red portent.
translations.idiomatic: This was a red omen.

sentences.zh: 是時後將軍褚裒鎮廣陵，丞相揚聲北伐，伯以督運稽留及役使臧罪，依征軍法戮之。

translations.literal: At that time Rear General Chu Pou garrisoned Guangling; the Chancellor loudly proclaimed a northern campaign; Bo, for delay in supervising transport and the crime of embezzling laborers, was executed according to the punitive military law.
translations.idiomatic: Rear General Chu Pou then garrisoned Guangling while the Chancellor proclaimed a northern expedition; Bo was executed under wartime law for delays in supply transport and forcing laborers for private gain.

sentences.zh: 其息訴稱：「伯督運事訖，無所稽乏，受賕役使，罪不及死。

translations.literal: His son appealed claiming: "Bo finished supervising transport affairs and there was nothing delayed or lacking; accepting bribes and using laborers—the crime did not reach death.
translations.idiomatic: His son protested: "My father had completed the transport mission without delay or shortfall; though he took bribes and forced labor, the offense did not warrant death.

sentences.zh: 兵家之勢，先聲後實，實是屯戍，非為征軍。

translations.literal: In military affairs the pattern is first reputation, then substance; the substance here was garrison duty, not a campaign army.
translations.idiomatic: In military affairs fame precedes substance; the substance here was garrison duty, not a field army on campaign.

sentences.zh: 自四年以來，運漕稽停，皆不以軍興法論。

translations.literal: Since the fourth year, transport and grain shipments have been delayed, yet none of this is judged by the laws for raising armies.
translations.idiomatic: Since the fourth year transport convoys have been delayed, yet none of this is judged under the laws for raising armies.

sentences.zh: 」僚佐莫之理。

translations.literal: " None of the staff officials would heed this.
translations.idiomatic: " No one among the staff would listen.
